definition_zh: 康塔塔；大合唱（声乐套曲）
definition_en: a musical composition for voices and instruments in several movements, usually on a sacred or dramatic text
core_image: 唱出来的 Sonata：歌手站成一排，管风琴托底，一乐章接一乐章地唱完一个故事
scene: 教堂晨光斜照进彩窗，唱诗班在管风琴前整队。 The choir rehearsed Bach's Easter cantata for the holiday service.
sceneCN: 这里 cantata 是「康塔塔」（第 1 个义项：多乐章声乐套曲）；句意是唱诗班为节日礼拜排练巴赫的复活节康塔塔。

pos.zh: 康塔塔（多乐章声乐套曲）
（泛指）大型合唱作品

collocations.phrase: a cantata for soloists and chorus
collocations.zh: 为独唱与合唱而作的康塔塔

derivatives.zh: 复合形容词，义为「康塔塔风格的」
同根音乐术语，义为「如歌的」（意大利语 cantare 同根）
对偶借词，义为「奏鸣曲」（同一构词模式，乐器版）

senses.title: A multi-movement vocal work with instruments
senses.definition: a composition for one or more voices with instrumental accompaniment, in several movements, often on a religious text
senses.definitionCN: 为独唱或合唱配器乐伴奏、分多个乐章的作品，常取宗教题材
senses.example: The church cantata alternates arias with choruses.
senses.exampleCN: 这首教堂康塔塔在咏叹调与合唱之间交替。
senses.why: The Italian name means sung piece, the voice-side twin of the played sonata.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语原名意为「唱的作品」，是「奏的」奏鸣曲在声乐一侧的孪生词。

senses.title: A large-scale choral composition generally
senses.definition: in loose modern use, any substantial work for chorus, soloists, and orchestra
senses.definitionCN: 现代宽泛用法中，泛指为合唱、独唱与乐队而作的大型作品
senses.example: The festival commissioned a cantata honoring the city's founders.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐节委约了一部致敬城市奠基者的康塔塔。
senses.why: Once a genre name, it broadens to cover the family of sung multi-part works.
senses.whyCN: 它本是体裁名，随后扩展覆盖「多乐章声乐作品」这一整个家族。

intro.en: Cantata is the Italian feminine past participle of cantare, to sing, coined in the seventeenth century as the sung counterpart of the sonata, the played piece.
intro.cn: cantata 是意大利语 cantare（歌唱）的阴性过去分词，十七世纪被造出，作为「演奏的」sonata 在声乐一方的对应词。

items.en: The root *kan- means to sing or chant, ancient and widespread across Indo-European.
items.cn: 词根 *kan- 意为歌唱、吟诵，古老且遍布印欧诸语。

items.en: Latin cantare is the frequentative of canere, to sing, giving chant, cantor, and incantation.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cantare 是 canere（歌唱）的反复动词形式，衍生出 chant、cantor、incantation。

items.en: Italian composers coined cantata da cantarsi, a piece to be sung, against sonata, a piece to be sounded.
items.cn: 意大利作曲家造出 cantata da cantarsi（供演唱之作），与 sonata（供演奏之作）相对。

items.en: English borrowed the term in the early eighteenth century as Italian church music spread north.
items.cn: 十八世纪初，随着意大利宗教音乐北传，英语借入了这一术语。

items.en: Today it names both the Baroque church genre and modern festival choral commissions.
items.cn: 如今它既指巴洛克教堂体裁，也指现代音乐节的委约合唱作品。

note.en: Cantata belongs to the singing family of cant- words and to the sonata pairing.
note.cn: cantata 属于 cant-「歌唱」词族，并与 sonata 构成一对。

entries.definition: A multi-movement work for instruments, the played twin of the sung cantata.
entries.definitionCN: 多乐章器乐作品，是「唱的」康塔塔的「奏的」孪生词。

entries.definition: In a singing style, a direction for instrumental players.
entries.definitionCN: 如歌地，给器乐演奏者的表情术语，同根。

entries.definition: The leader of congregational singing, especially in synagogues and churches.
entries.definitionCN: 领唱者，尤指犹太会堂或教堂中的领唱。

entries.definition: Chanted words believed to have magical power.
entries.definitionCN: 咒语；念诵的祷文，同根。

entries.definition: A large sacred choral drama, longer and more theatrical than a cantata.
entries.definitionCN: 大型宗教合唱剧，篇幅与戏剧性超过康塔塔。

entries.definition: A Lutheran hymn tune, the building block of many cantatas.
entries.definitionCN: 路德宗众赞歌，许多康塔塔的素材来源。

entries.definition: A polyphonic choral work, usually unaccompanied.
entries.definitionCN: 复调合唱作品，通常无伴奏。

entries.definition: A solo song within an opera or cantata.
entries.definitionCN: 咏叹调，歌剧或康塔塔中的独唱段落。

entries.definition: The purely instrumental large form, no singing required.
entries.definitionCN: 纯器乐的大型体裁，无需人声，与 cantata 形成对照。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the sing root and the sonata pairing.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「歌唱」词根与 sonata 配对关系的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Root core: Italian cantata means a piece that is sung, from cantare.
normal.cn: 词根核心：意大利语 cantata 意为「唱出来的作品」，出自 cantare。

normal.en: Twin pair: sonata sounds, cantata sings; one letter separates the pair.
normal.cn: 孪生配对：sonata 奏、cantata 唱，两个词只差一个字母。

normal.en: Genre ladder: aria inside cantata inside oratorio, pieces nesting by size.
normal.cn: 体裁阶梯：aria 在 cantata 之内，cantata 在 oratorio 之内，按规模层层嵌套。

normal.en: Composer hook: Bach wrote over two hundred church cantatas for the Leipzig calendar.
normal.cn: 作曲家钩子：巴赫为莱比锡的礼拜年历写了二百多首教堂康塔塔。

normal.en: Family chorus: chant, cantor, cantabile, incantation all live on cant-.
normal.cn: 家族合唱：chant、cantor、cantabile、incantation 都住在 cant- 词根上。

abstract.en: Voices and organ braided together, one movement handing the story to the next.
abstract.cn: 人声与管风琴交织，一个乐章把故事递给下一个乐章。

abstract.en: A hall where the score itself seems to breathe, inhaling at the arias and exhaling in chorus.
abstract.cn: 一座乐谱仿佛在呼吸的音乐厅：咏叹调吸气，合唱吐气。

abstract.en: Two doors in one corridor: this side sings, that side plays.
abstract.cn: 同一条走廊上的两扇门：这边唱，那边奏。

examples.en: The high school choir performed a spring cantata for the town.
examples.cn: 高中合唱团为全镇演出了一部春季康塔塔。

examples.en: Scholars catalogued the cantatas by liturgical calendar.
examples.cn: 学者们按礼拜年历为这些康塔塔编目。

examples.en: Her aria floated above the orchestra in the cantata's second movement.
examples.cn: 康塔塔第二乐章里，她的咏叹调在乐队之上飘浮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坎塔塔」——站在坎（坎）台上又唱「塔塔」两声，台上人声一波接一波，正是多乐章的大合唱康塔塔；联想 sonata 是奏鸣曲，cantata 就是「唱鸣曲」。

root: 源自意大利语 cantata（cantare「歌唱」的阴性过去分词），可上溯至拉丁语 cantare（canere 的反复体），一般认为出自印欧词根 *kan-（歌唱）。十七世纪意大利作曲家以 cantata（唱的作品）与 sonata（奏的作品）相对；英语于十八世纪初借入。同根词有 chant、cantor、cantabile、incantation。

sensesIntro.en: From the Baroque sung piece the name widens to any substantial multi-part choral work.
sensesIntro.cn: 从巴洛克的声乐套曲出发，这一名称扩展为泛指一切大型多声部合唱作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: voices in movements, a story sung from first aria to final chorus.
core.cn: 核心意象：分乐章的人声，一个从首段咏叹调唱到终曲合唱的故事。

branches.en: THE LOFT: the Baroque church cantata over the congregation.
branches.cn: 唱诗楼：高悬于会众之上的巴洛克教堂康塔塔。

branches.en: THE PODIUM: modern choral commissions on secular themes.
branches.cn: 指挥台：世俗题材的现代委约合唱作品。

branches.en: THE ARCHITECTURE: arias, recitatives, and choruses stacked like floors.
branches.cn: 建筑结构：咏叹调、宣叙调与合唱如楼层般堆叠。

branches.en: THE PAIRING: sonata plays what cantata sings.
branches.cn: 配对关系：sonata 所奏即 cantata 所唱。

branches.en: THE OCCASION: civic and seasonal ceremonies borrowing the sacred form.
branches.cn: 场合：市民与节庆仪式借用这一宗教形式。

intro.en: Cantata is the Italian past participle of cantare, sung, one half of the sing-play naming pair.
intro.cn: cantata 是意大利语 cantare 的过去分词「被唱的」，是「唱-奏」命名配对的一半。

latinIntro.en: The cantare root of repeated singing feeds a wide sacred and musical family.
latinIntro.cn: cantare（反复歌唱）词根滋养出一个庞大的宗教与音乐词族。

items.exampleCN: 罗马仪式中的歌唱（拉丁语用例示意）。
在民众面前歌唱（拉丁语用例示意）。

items.meaningCN: 被完成的（意大利语分词词尾）

items.exampleCN: 以如歌的方式奏出旋律。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 她爱歌唱（拉丁语用例示意）。

definition_zh: 情感的；情绪的；表达情感的（心理学中与认知相对）
definition_en: relating to moods, feelings and attitudes rather than to thought; in psychology, concerned with emotion as opposed to cognition
core_image: 事情先在心里起了波澜，然后才被说出来
scene: 量表上分开的两栏，一栏问记得多少，一栏问感觉如何。 The test measures affective response, not memory.
sceneCN: 这里 affective 是「情感的」（第 1 个义项：与情绪、感受有关，心理学中与认知相对）；句意为该测试测量的是情感反应而非记忆。核心画面是事情先在心里起了波澜。

pos.zh: 情感的；情绪的

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「影响；感动」，读作 /əˈfekt/
同根名词，义为「喜爱；感情」
加 -ly 构成，义为「在情感上」

senses.title: Relating to emotion rather than thought
senses.definition: in psychology, concerned with feelings, moods and attitudes, as opposed to cognitive processes
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学中，与感受、心境和态度有关，与认知过程相对
senses.example: Seasonal affective disorder lifts as the days lengthen.
senses.exampleCN: 季节性情感障碍随白昼变长而缓解。
senses.why: Afficere means to do something to a person, so affective describes what has been done to the inner state: the mind moved rather than informed.
senses.whyCN: afficere 意为「对一个人施加作用」，所以 affective 描述的是内在状态被作用之后的样子：心被打动，而不是被告知。

senses.title: Expressing or carrying feeling
senses.definition: of language, art or behaviour, conveying emotion rather than information
senses.definitionCN: 指语言、艺术或行为传达情感而非信息
senses.example: The poem is affective rather than descriptive.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗重抒情而非描写。
senses.why: The same being-acted-upon image turns outward: what was felt inside is now carried by words or colour to someone else.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「被作用」的意象转向外部：内在感受到的东西，如今由词语或色彩传递给另一个人。

intro.en: Affective comes from doing something to someone: Latin facere, to do, is the engine, and the prefix ad- aims it at a person.
intro.cn: affective 来自「对某人施加作用」：拉丁语 facere「做」是引擎，前缀 ad- 把它对准一个人。

items.en: Facere meant to do or to make, and it gives English fact, factory, effect and perfect.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、制造」，它给出英语 fact、factory、effect 与 perfect。

items.en: Afficere joined ad-, to, with facere, meaning to do something to, to influence or to move.
items.cn: afficere 把 ad-「向」与 facere 结合，义为「对……施加作用、影响、打动」。

items.en: Affectus, the past participle, named a state or disposition, especially of the mind.
items.cn: affectus 是过去分词，指一种状态或心境，尤指心理状态。

items.en: French affectif carried the sense of relating to the emotions into learned writing.
items.cn: 法语 affectif 把「与情感有关」的意义带入学术文体。

items.en: English affective is recorded from the fifteenth century and is now chiefly a technical term in psychology and education.
items.cn: 英语 affective 见于十五世纪，如今主要是心理学与教育学中的术语。

note.en: The look-alike group warns about effective, which differs by one letter and means something quite different; the near-meaning group lists other words for feeling.
note.cn: 形近组提醒 effective 只差一个字母而意义大不相同；近义组列出其他表示情感的词。

entries.definition: Producing the intended result; not about feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 产生预期效果的；与情感无关。

entries.definition: A gentle feeling of fondness.
entries.definitionCN: 温柔的喜爱之情。

entries.definition: Behaviour that is artificial and meant to impress.
entries.definitionCN: 做作、意在给人印象的行为。

entries.definition: Relating to or showing strong feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 与强烈感情有关或表现强烈感情的。

entries.definition: Arousing feeling, especially in language.
entries.definitionCN: 激起感情的，尤指语言。

entries.definition: Relating to thought and knowing, the usual opposite in psychology.
entries.definitionCN: 与思维和认知有关，心理学中通常的反面。

normalIntro.en: Keep affective and effective apart: affective has the a of affect, effective has the e of effect.
normalIntro.cn: 把 affective 与 effective 分开：affective 带 affect 的 a，effective 带 effect 的 e。

normal.en: Affect is the verb about feelings; affective is its adjective.
normal.cn: affect 是关于情感的动词；affective 是它的形容词。

normal.en: Effect is a result; effective means it works. Affect is a feeling; affective means it feels.
normal.cn: effect 是结果，effective 表示有效；affect 是感受，affective 表示情感。

normal.en: Affective disorder is a mood disorder, not a disorder that works well.
normal.cn: affective disorder 是心境障碍，不是「运转良好的障碍」。

normal.en: The affective domain in teaching covers attitudes, not facts.
normal.cn: 教学中的情感领域涵盖态度，而非事实。

normal.en: Affectively is the adverb, though emotional is more common in speech.
normal.cn: affectively 是副词，不过口语中 emotional 更常见。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped into water: the rings are the affective part.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头落入水中：涟漪就是情感的那部分。

abstract.en: Imagine two columns on a form, one asking what you know and one asking how you feel.
abstract.cn: 想象表格上两栏，一栏问你知道什么，一栏问你感觉如何。

abstract.en: Think of a sentence that carries warmth rather than information.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传递温度而非信息的句子。

examples.en: The researchers separated cognitive scores from affective ones.
examples.cn: 研究者把认知得分与情感得分分开。

examples.en: Music has an affective power that argument lacks.
examples.cn: 音乐具有论证所缺乏的情感力量。

examples.en: Affective bonds form long before language does.
examples.cn: 情感纽带远在语言之前就已形成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「额飞克提夫」——额（af）飞（fec）克提夫（tive），心里先飞起一阵波澜，再被说出来，就是情感的。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 facere「做」构成 afficere「对……施加作用、打动」，其过去分词 affectus 指心境状态，加形容词后缀 -ive 构成 affective，字面即「与被打动的状态有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses keep the image of an inner state being acted upon: first as something felt inside, then as something carried outward by words or art.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都保留「内在状态被作用」的意象：先是内在感受到的东西，再是由词语或艺术向外传递的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an inner state that has been moved
core.cn: 核心意象：被拨动的内在状态

branches.en: The state studied as mood and attitude.
branches.cn: 作为心境与态度被研究的状态。

branches.en: The state carried outward by art.
branches.cn: 由艺术向外传递的状态。

branches.en: Both stand opposite to cognitive.
branches.cn: 两者都与 cognitive 相对。

branches.en: The technical sense used in diagnosis.
branches.cn: 用于诊断的术语义。

branches.en: The sense used of poems and music.
branches.cn: 用于诗歌与音乐的意义。

intro.en: Affective belongs to the huge facere family, where the prefix decides whether the doing is aimed at a person or at a result.
intro.cn: affective 属于庞大的 facere 词族，前缀决定这份「做」是对准一个人还是对准一个结果。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus facere gave afficere and affectus; ex- plus the same root gave effectus, which is why affective and effective look so alike.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 facere 产生 afficere 与 affectus；ex- 加同一词根产生 effectus，这正是 affective 与 effective 如此相像的原因。

latinEntries.example: Facere is the root of affect and effect.
latinEntries.exampleCN: facere 是 affect 与 effect 的词根。
affectus 是 affective 的来源。

definition_zh: 自然主义的；写实的；自然情境下的；博物学的；自然题材的
definition_en: relating to naturalism, or representing nature and life as they actually are rather than as one might wish them to be
core_image: 画室里没有人摆姿势，画家把画架搬到田边，画布上留着杂草、泥痕和斜斜的日光。
scene: 美术馆导览员站在一幅乡村画前说，这位画家拒绝把田野画成理想化的风景，只如实记录泥泞、杂草和斜照的光。 The painter kept the field naturalistic, showing mud and weeds instead of an ideal view.
sceneCN: 这里 naturalistic 是“以自然主义方式如实再现现实”（第 1 个义项）；句意：画家把这片田野画得写实，画的是泥泞与杂草，而不是理想化的景色。

pos.zh: 自然主义的；写实的；自然情境下的；博物学的；自然题材的

senses.title: The style that copies life
senses.titleCN: 自然主义：把生活原样搬上画布
senses.definition: relating to naturalism in art or literature, which shows life and nature as they are without idealizing them
senses.definitionCN: 属于文学艺术中的自然主义，如实呈现生活与自然而不作美化
senses.example: The novel is naturalistic in its refusal to give its poor characters a happy ending.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是自然主义的，它拒绝给贫穷的人物一个圆满结局。
senses.why: Naturalism claims that environment and heredity decide human fate; a naturalistic work therefore records causes and conditions instead of arranging a pleasing outcome.
senses.whyCN: 自然主义主张环境与遗传决定人的命运；因此自然主义作品记录原因与条件，而不安排一个讨喜的结局。

senses.title: Lifelike, close to the real
senses.titleCN: 写实逼真：看起来就像真的
senses.definition: resembling real life closely in appearance, sound, or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 在外观、声音或行为上非常接近真实生活
senses.example: The film's naturalistic dialogue made the actors sound like people we know.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片的写实对白让演员听起来像我们认识的人。
senses.why: Here naturalistic judges resemblance, not theory: the test is whether a viewer feels the thing before them could exist outside the frame.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 naturalistic 判断的是相似度而非理论：标准是观众是否觉得眼前之物在画框之外也可能存在。

senses.title: Studied in the wild
senses.titleCN: 自然情境下：不在实验室里观察
senses.definition: describing research carried out in ordinary surroundings rather than in a controlled laboratory
senses.definitionCN: 指在日常生活环境中而非受控实验室里进行的研究
senses.example: Naturalistic observation recorded how children actually share toys in the playground.
senses.exampleCN: 自然情境观察记录了儿童在操场上实际如何分享玩具。
senses.why: The setting itself becomes part of the method: to see behaviour as it naturally occurs, the researcher must give up control over the conditions.
senses.whyCN: 环境本身成了方法的一部分：要看行为自然发生的样子，研究者必须放弃对条件的控制。

senses.title: Belonging to natural history
senses.titleCN: 博物学的：记录花草虫鸟的学问
senses.definition: relating to the description and study of plants, animals, and minerals in their habitats
senses.definitionCN: 与在栖息地中描述和研究动植物、矿物有关
senses.example: The museum's naturalistic drawings date from an age before photography.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆里的博物学绘图来自摄影术出现之前的年代。
senses.why: Natural history was once the study of everything under nature; its drawings are called naturalistic because accuracy to the specimen, not beauty, is the aim.
senses.whyCN: 博物学曾经研究自然中的一切；其绘图被称作 naturalistic，因为目标是忠实于标本，而不是美观。

senses.title: Nature is all there is
senses.titleCN: 自然主义哲学：只承认自然存在
senses.definition: holding the philosophical view that nature is the whole of reality and needs no supernatural explanation
senses.definitionCN: 持这样一种哲学观点：自然就是全部现实，无需超自然解释
senses.example: A naturalistic account of mind tries to explain thought without appealing to anything beyond nature.
senses.exampleCN: 对心灵的自然主义解释试图不借助自然之外的东西来说明思想。
senses.why: This sense moves the word from style to worldview: whatever exists must be accounted for within nature, so the natural is the boundary of what can be discussed.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把词从风格移到世界观：凡存在的都须在自然之内解释，因此“自然”成了可讨论之物的边界。

senses.title: Plain, without polish
senses.titleCN: 平实不加修饰：不替现实打光
senses.definition: presented in a plain, matter-of-fact way that leaves out decoration or idealization
senses.definitionCN: 以平实、就事论事的方式呈现，去掉装饰与理想化
senses.example: He gave a naturalistic account of the accident, including the parts that made him look careless.
senses.exampleCN: 他平实地叙述了那场事故，连让他显得粗心的部分也没有省略。
senses.why: When decoration is removed, what remains is claimed to be nature itself; plainness becomes evidence of honesty rather than a lack of skill.
senses.whyCN: 去掉装饰后，剩下的被主张为自然本身；朴素由此成了诚实的证据，而不是技巧的欠缺。

senses.title: Motifs borrowed from nature
senses.titleCN: 自然题材：把枝叶花鸟搬进图案
senses.definition: using plants, animals, or landscapes as decorative motifs
senses.definitionCN: 以植物、动物或风景作为装饰母题
senses.example: The wallpaper has a naturalistic pattern of ivy and small birds.
senses.exampleCN: 墙纸上是常春藤和小鸟的自然题材图案。
senses.why: Decorative arts borrow the shapes of living things but flatten them into repeatable patterns; naturalistic marks the source of the motif, not the realism of the wall.
senses.whyCN: 装饰艺术借用生物的形态，却把它们压平成可重复的图案；naturalistic 标的是母题的来源，而不是墙面的写实程度。

senses.title: Unforced and unstudied
senses.titleCN: 自然不做作：举止里没有排练
senses.definition: behaving in an easy, unforced way that does not seem planned or performed
senses.definitionCN: 举止轻松自然，看不出刻意安排或表演的痕迹
senses.example: Her naturalistic manner put the interviewees at ease.
senses.exampleCN: 她自然不做作的举止让受访者放松下来。
senses.why: A performance becomes naturalistic when the audience stops noticing the performance; the word then praises the absence of visible effort.
senses.whyCN: 当观众不再注意到“表演”时，表演就变得 naturalistic；此时这个词赞美的是看不见的用力痕迹。

intro.en: Naturalistic joins natural with the Greek-derived suffix -istic. The base is Latin natura, from nasci, to be born.
intro.cn: naturalistic 由 natural 与源自希腊语的后缀 -istic 组合而成。词基是拉丁语 natura，出自 nasci“出生”。

items.en: Nasci meant to be born. Its noun natura named the course of things at birth, hence the character of the world and of a person.
items.cn: nasci 意为“出生”。其名词 natura 指出生时带来的禀性，进而指世界的本性以及人的天性。

items.en: Naturalis meant belonging to nature or produced by it, as opposed to what is made by art or by human arrangement.
items.cn: naturalis 意为“属于自然的、由自然产生的”，与人工或人为安排相对。

items.en: Old French naturel carried both the outward sense of the physical world and the inward sense of inborn character.
items.cn: 古法语 naturel 同时承载“外在物质世界”与“内在固有性格”两层意思。

items.en: English natural covers what is not artificial, what is inborn, and what is simply normal or expected.
items.cn: 英语 natural 涵盖“非人工的”“天生的”以及“正常、理所当然的”三层意思。

items.en: The suffix came through French -istique from Greek -istikos. It forms adjectives naming a style, a doctrine, or a practice.
items.cn: 该后缀经法语 -istique 来自希腊语 -istikos，用来构成表示风格、学说或做法的形容词。

items.en: Naturalistic is recorded in the mid-19th century, first for art that follows nature closely, then for the philosophical view that nature is all of reality.
items.cn: naturalistic 的书面记录见于 19 世纪中期，最初指紧贴自然的艺术，随后指“自然即全部现实”的哲学观点。

note.en: The first group is the word family built on nature; the second compares styles and methods that claim to follow reality.
note.cn: 第一组是基于 nature 的词族；第二组比较几种自称“追随现实”的风格与方法。

entries.definition: existing in nature, not made by people; also inborn or normal. It states a fact about origin.
entries.definitionCN: 自然界存在、非人造的；也指天生的或正常的。它陈述的是来源事实。

entries.definition: the artistic movement or philosophical view that nature is the whole of reality. It names the doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 主张自然即全部现实的艺术运动或哲学观点；它命名的是学说。

entries.definition: a person who studies plants and animals in the field, or an artist who works in the naturalistic style.
entries.definitionCN: 在野外研究动植物的人，或采用自然主义风格的艺术家。

entries.definition: showing things as they are and accepting practical limits. It often also means sensible about what is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 如实呈现事物并接受现实限制；也常指对可能性抱务实态度。

entries.definition: looking or sounding exactly like a living thing. It judges surface resemblance only.
entries.definitionCN: 外观或声音酷似活物；只判断表面的相似度。

entries.definition: extremely detailed and exact in art, especially Italian portraiture. It stresses precision of detail rather than social theory.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术上极为精细写实，尤指意大利肖像；强调细节精确而非社会理论。

entries.definition: based on watching and recording rather than experiment. It names the method, not the style.
entries.definitionCN: 基于观察记录而非实验；命名的是方法，而不是风格。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: nature plus -istic. The suffix says 'in the manner of', so naturalistic means 'in the manner of nature'.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：nature 加 -istic。后缀表示“以……的方式”，所以 naturalistic 就是“以自然的方式”。

normal.en: Nature + -istic: in the manner of nature, with no makeup added.
normal.cn: nature 加 -istic：以自然的方式，不额外化妆。

normal.en: A naturalistic play ends where life would end, not where the audience would like it to.
normal.cn: 自然主义的戏剧在生活本该结束的地方结束，而不是在观众希望的地方结束。

normal.en: In psychology, naturalistic means the playground instead of the lab.
normal.cn: 在心理学里，naturalistic 意味着操场而不是实验室。

normal.en: On wallpaper, naturalistic ivy is still a pattern, not a plant.
normal.cn: 墙纸上的自然题材常春藤仍是图案，不是植物。

normal.en: A naturalistic manner is one where you cannot see the rehearsing.
normal.cn: 自然不做作的举止，就是你看不出排练痕迹的那种举止。

abstract.en: To call something naturalistic is to claim that no hand has improved it, and that claim is itself an artistic decision.
abstract.cn: 说某物是自然主义的，就是宣称没有手笔修饰过它；而这个宣称本身就是一次艺术决定。

abstract.en: Nature never presents itself unedited; every naturalistic work chooses which parts of nature to keep.
abstract.cn: 自然从不以未经剪辑的样子出现；每件自然主义作品都在选择保留自然的哪些部分。

abstract.en: The word holds a quiet argument: if nature is all there is, then explaining anything means staying inside it.
abstract.cn: 这个词里藏着一场安静的争论：若自然就是全部，那么解释任何事物都必须留在自然之内。

examples.en: The director shot the factory in naturalistic light, so the machines looked heavy and the faces tired.
examples.cn: 导演用自然主义的光拍摄工厂，机器显得沉重，人脸显得疲惫。

examples.en: A naturalistic study in the classroom found that children help each other more than tests suggest.
examples.cn: 一项在教室里进行的自然情境研究发现了比测验结果更多的儿童互助行为。

examples.en: The naturalistic explanation of religion treats belief as a product of human minds and societies.
examples.cn: 对宗教的自然主义解释把信仰看作人类心智与社会的产物。

dict_mnemonic.text: natural（自然的）+ istic（风格）——照着自然画，不加滤镜，就是自然主义的。

root: 由 natural（自然的，源自拉丁语 natura“出生、本性”）加希腊语来源的后缀 -istic（以……方式、属于……派）构成，本义为“以自然为本、按自然的样子呈现”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of naturalistic, all circling one idea: nature supplies the standard. The standard may be a subject to be copied, a setting to be preserved, a doctrine to be defended, or a manner to be kept unforced.
sensesIntro.cn: naturalistic 的八个义项都围绕一个观念：以自然为标准。这个标准可以是被临摹的对象、被保留的环境、被辩护的学说，或被保持为不做作的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an easel in a field, paint recording mud, weeds, and slanting light without cleaning them up.
core.cn: 核心意象：田边的画架，画布记录泥泞、杂草与斜光，一样也不修饰。

chain: NATURALISTIC REPRESENTING IN THE MANNER OF NATURE

branches.en: ART WITHOUT POLISH: the movement that refuses idealization and the plain account that refuses decoration.
branches.cn: 不加修饰的艺术：拒绝理想化的流派，与拒绝装饰的平实叙述。

branches.en: RESEMBLANCE IN MANNER: lifelike dialogue and unforced behaviour both make the artificial invisible.
branches.cn: 方式上的相似：写实对白与不做作的举止，都让人为痕迹消失。

branches.en: NATURE AS METHOD: fieldwork in ordinary settings and natural-history drawing both let the object set the terms.
branches.cn: 以自然为方法：日常环境中的田野研究与博物学绘图，都让对象决定规则。

branches.en: NATURE AS REALITY: the philosophical claim that nothing exists beyond the natural order.
branches.cn: 以自然为现实：哲学上主张自然秩序之外别无存在。

branches.en: NATURE AS SOURCE OF FORM: decorative motifs borrowed from plants and animals.
branches.cn: 以自然为形式来源：从动植物借来的装饰母题。

intro.en: Naturalistic is natural plus -istic, a suffix that turns a noun or adjective into a style label. The family then adds -ism for the doctrine and -ist for the person.
intro.cn: naturalistic 是 natural 加 -istic；该后缀把名词或形容词变成风格标签。词族再用 -ism 表示学说、用 -ist 表示人。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is nasci, to be born, with the noun natura and the adjective naturalis. Greek -istikos supplies the style suffix through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 nasci“出生”，名词 natura，形容词 naturalis。风格后缀则经法语来自希腊语 -istikos。

items.meaning: the physical world, or the inborn character of a thing
items.meaningCN: 自然界；或事物的固有本性
items.example: The nature of the soil decides which plants survive.
items.exampleCN: 土壤的性质决定哪些植物能存活。

items.meaning: produced by nature, not by people; inborn; normal
items.meaningCN: 自然产生的、非人造的；天生的；正常的
items.example: The cave is a natural shelter, not a built one.
items.exampleCN: 这个洞穴是天然庇护所，不是人造的。

items.meaning: the view that nature is all of reality, or the art movement that follows it
items.meaningCN: 自然即全部现实的学说，或追随该主张的艺术运动
items.example: Naturalism in the novel replaced heroic plots with ordinary lives.
items.exampleCN: 小说中的自然主义用普通人的生活取代英雄情节。

items.meaning: a field researcher of plants and animals, or a follower of naturalism
items.meaningCN: 野外研究动植物的学者，或自然主义的追随者
items.example: The naturalist spent a year recording birds in the marsh.
items.exampleCN: 这位博物学家用一年时间记录沼泽里的鸟类。

items.meaning: resembling nature or following the naturalist style
items.meaningCN: 类似自然的；遵循自然主义风格的
items.example: The exhibit pairs naturalistic drawings with living specimens.
items.exampleCN: 展览把博物学绘图与活体标本配对陈列。

items.meaning: in a manner that copies nature closely
items.meaningCN: 以贴近自然的方式；写实地
items.example: The animals were painted naturalistically, down to the mud on their legs.
items.exampleCN: 这些动物被画得很写实，连腿上的泥都画了出来。

items.meaningCN: 超自然的；自然秩序之外的
items.exampleCN: 自然主义否认任何超自然原因。

items.meaning: contrary to nature or to normal feeling
items.example: The silence in the forest felt unnatural.
items.exampleCN: 森林里的寂静让人觉得反常。

items.meaning: to make something natural, or to adopt a plant, word, or person as native
items.meaningCN: 使自然化；使（植物、词语、人）归化
items.example: The shrub naturalized itself along the river within a decade.
items.exampleCN: 这种灌木十年内就在河边归化了。

latinEntries.meaning: to be born, to arise, to grow

scene: 画家支起画架，山坡上牛群懒懒地嚼草。 He spent the summer painting bucolic scenes of the valley.

senses.title: Of the pleasant countryside
senses.titleCN: 田园风光的；乡野宜人的
senses.definition: relating to the attractive, simple aspects of rural life and scenery
senses.definitionCN: 与乡村生活及景致中质朴宜人的一面相关
senses.example: They traded the city for a bucolic farmhouse.
senses.exampleCN: 他们抛下城市，换了一座田园农舍。
senses.why: The Greek root boukolos is a cowherd; herding life stands for idealized country scenes.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根 boukolos 意为牧牛人，放牧生活成为理想化乡村的代称。

senses.title: Of pastoral poetry
senses.definition: relating to poetry or literature that idealizes shepherd life
senses.definitionCN: 与美化牧人生活的诗歌文学相关
senses.example: Virgil's bucolic verse shaped the whole tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 维吉尔的牧歌奠定了整个传统。
senses.why: The cowherd moved from the field to the page: rural subjects became a literary genre.
senses.whyCN: 牧牛人从田野走上书页，乡村题材凝定为一种文学体裁，义项由景入文。

senses.title: A pastoral poem
senses.definition: a short poem about rural or shepherd life
senses.definitionCN: 以乡村或牧人生活为题材的短诗
senses.example: The anthology reprints fifteen bucolics.
senses.exampleCN: 这部选集重印了十五首牧歌。
senses.why: An adjective of genre slips into a noun naming the work itself.
senses.whyCN: 表体裁的形容词顺势转指作品本身，完成由形容到名词的转化。

senses.title: Rustic and unsophisticated
senses.titleCN: 乡土气的；土里土气的（略带贬义）
senses.definition: suggesting the countryside in a way that seems simple or unsophisticated
senses.definitionCN: 带有乡土气息，显得质朴甚至缺乏教养
senses.example: His bucolic manners amused the city guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他土气的做派把城里客人逗乐了。
senses.why: What the city idealizes as charm, it also patronizes as rusticity.
senses.whyCN: 城市既把乡土美化为魅力，也把它俯视为土气，义项由褒转贬。

intro.en: Bucolic descends from Greek boukolikos, the adjective of boukolos, a cowherd.
intro.cn: bucolic 源自希腊语 boukolikos，即 boukolos（牧牛人）的形容词。

items.en: a reconstructed root gwou fed the words for ox and cow.
items.cn: 重构词根 gwou 滋生出表示牛的一族词。

items.en: bous meant ox and boukolos a cowherd, then boukolikos meant pastoral.
items.cn: 希腊语 bous 为牛，boukolos 为牧牛人，boukolikos 义为田园牧歌的。

items.en: bucolicus kept the literary sense in Virgil's pastoral world.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bucolicus 在维吉尔的牧歌世界中沿用文学义。

items.en: bucolic entered English for pastoral poetry, then widened to rural scenery.
items.cn: bucolic 进入英语先指田园诗，后扩展到乡村景致。

items.en: bucolic now paints the countryside as charming, sometimes quaintly backward.
items.cn: 如今 bucolic 描绘乡村之美，有时带几分土气戏谑。

note.en: Bucolic shares a cow-root family and stands beside its pastoral and rustic neighbors.
note.cn: bucolic 与同出「牛」词根的词为一家，并邻接 pastoral、rustic 等近义词。

entries.definition: writing that turns like oxen plowing
entries.definitionCN: 牛耕式书写，同含希腊语 bous（牛）

entries.definition: idealizing shepherd and rural life
entries.definitionCN: 田园牧歌的，近义核心词

entries.definition: simple and rural, sometimes crude
entries.definitionCN: 乡土的，朴拙的

entries.definition: a musical or dramatic rural piece
entries.definitionCN: 田园曲，田园剧

normalIntro.cn: 拆开希腊语：bou（牛）加 kolos（放牧人）画面即出。

normal.en: The cow sound sits right at the front: bu-co-lic.
normal.cn: 「牛」的音就压在开头：bu-co-lic。

normal.en: A cowherd playing a flute is the root image.
normal.cn: 核心画面：吹笛的牧牛人。

normal.en: Pastoral is its Latin twin, from shepherd.
normal.cn: pastoral 是它的拉丁孪生词，来自牧羊人。

normal.en: Georgic is the farming twin, bucolic the herding one.
normal.cn: georgic 管农事，bucolic 管放牧。

normal.en: The noun bucolics names the poems themselves.
normal.cn: 名词 bucolics 指那些牧歌作品。

abstract.en: Hear a flute float over a slow-moving herd.
abstract.cn: 听笛声在缓缓移动的牛群上空飘荡。

abstract.en: Feel afternoon sun warm a hillside of grass.
abstract.cn: 感受午后阳光晒暖一片山坡。

abstract.en: See smoke rise straight from a thatched chimney.
abstract.cn: 看见炊烟从茅屋烟囱笔直升起。

examples.en: The novel opens with a bucolic description of harvest time.
examples.cn: 小说以 harvest 季节般的田园描写开场，写尽了乡野风光。

examples.en: City dwellers dream of a bucolic weekend in the hills.
examples.cn: 城里人向往在山间度过田园式的周末。

examples.en: The course compares ancient bucolics with modern nature writing.
examples.cn: 课程比较了古代牧歌与现代自然写作。

definition_en: water that falls from clouds as rain, snow, hail or sleet, or a solid that forms out of a solution
core_image: 云里的小水滴越聚越多，云托不住，一齐落向地面
scene: 山脊上的雨量筒一夜之间就积满了水。 Overnight precipitation filled the rain gauge on the ridge.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「从云中落到地面的水」（第 1 个义项：雨、雪、冰雹等从天而降的水）；句意为一夜之间的降水装满了山脊上的雨量筒。

pos.zh: 降水；降水量；（化学）沉淀；沉淀物；仓促

collocations.phrase: precipitation in the form of snow
collocations.zh: 以降雪形式出现的降水

derivatives.zh: 使沉淀；促成 / 沉淀物 / 仓促的

senses.title: Water falling from clouds
senses.definition: water that falls from the atmosphere to the ground
senses.definitionCN: 从大气降落到地面的水
senses.example: Overnight precipitation filled the rain gauge on the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一夜之间的降水装满了山脊上的雨量筒。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'to throw headlong'; the meteorologists' noun keeps that downward motion and applies it to water leaving the sky.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「头朝下抛落」；气象学的名词保留了这个向下动作，只是把落下的东西换成了离开天空的水。

senses.title: Snow, hail or sleet as forms of fall
senses.titleCN: 雪、冰雹、雨夹雪等降落形式
senses.definition: any form in which water falls, whether liquid or frozen
senses.definitionCN: 水降落的任何一种形态，无论液态还是冻结
senses.example: Winter precipitation in the mountains usually arrives as snow.
senses.exampleCN: 山区的冬季降水通常以雪的形式到来。
senses.why: Rain is only the commonest case; the word covers the whole class, so frozen forms count as the same event.
senses.whyCN: 雨只是最常见的一种；这个词覆盖整个类别，所以冻结形态也算同一种事件。

senses.title: The measured total
senses.definition: the amount of water that has fallen, usually measured in millimetres or inches
senses.definitionCN: 已经落下的水量，通常以毫米或英寸计
senses.example: The desert receives less than ten inches of precipitation a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沙漠每年降水不足十英寸。
senses.why: Once rain is caught in a gauge, the event turns into a quantity, and the same noun names the number.
senses.whyCN: 一旦雨被雨量筒接住，事件就变成了数量，同一个名词也就用来指这个数字。

senses.title: A solid forming in a solution
senses.definition: in chemistry, the process by which a dissolved substance becomes a solid
senses.definitionCN: 化学中指溶解的物质变成固体的过程
senses.example: Adding the salt caused precipitation of the dissolved silver.
senses.exampleCN: 加入这种盐使溶解的银发生了沉淀。
senses.why: A substance that was spread through a liquid suddenly stops being dissolved; it 'throws itself down' as a solid, the same image as rain leaving a cloud.
senses.whyCN: 原本分散在液体里的物质忽然不再溶解，以固体的形态「把自己抛下来」，与雨离开云是同一个意象。

senses.title: The solid that comes out
senses.definition: the solid material produced by that chemical process
senses.definitionCN: 该化学过程产生的固体物质
senses.example: The white precipitation was filtered off and dried.
senses.exampleCN: 白色沉淀物被滤出并烘干。
senses.why: English uses the same word for the process and for its product, because the product is simply the process seen as a finished thing.
senses.whyCN: 英语用同一个词既指过程也指产物，因为产物就是过程完成后被看作一个东西。

senses.title: A sudden onset of events
senses.definition: the act of making something happen suddenly or too soon
senses.definitionCN: 使某事突然或过早发生
senses.example: The report warns against precipitation of a trade war.
senses.exampleCN: 报告警告不要贸然引发贸易战。
senses.why: The old sense 'throwing headlong' moved from bodies to events: a crisis that is precipitated falls on people all at once.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「头朝下抛落」从身体移到了事件：被促成的危机一下子砸到人头上。

senses.title: Haste or rashness
senses.definition: the quality of acting too quickly, without enough thought
senses.definitionCN: 行动过快、思虑不足的性质
senses.example: He acted with precipitation and lost the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 他行事仓促，丢掉了那份合同。
senses.why: Someone who rushes is 'falling headlong' in behaviour rather than in body, so the metaphor becomes a judgement of character.
senses.whyCN: 匆忙的人是行为上「头朝下栽」，而非身体上，于是这个比喻变成对人的评价。

senses.title: The meteorological process
senses.definition: the whole process by which water vapour condenses and falls
senses.definitionCN: 水汽凝结并落下的整个过程
senses.example: Cold air over the lake increases precipitation along the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 湖面上的冷空气增加了沿岸的降水。
senses.why: This sense names the mechanism rather than the result, the same event viewed as a chain of steps.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项指机制而不是结果，是同一事件被看作一串步骤。

intro.en: Every sense goes back to one Latin verb meaning 'to throw headlong'. The word entered English through borrowed Latin, not through inheritance. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 所有义项都回到同一个拉丁动词，意为「头朝下抛落」。这个词经拉丁语借入英语，而非本土传承。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Latin praecipitatio meant 'a falling headlong' or 'haste', formed from praecipitare 'to throw down headlong'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 praecipitatio 意为「头朝下坠落」或「仓促」，由 praecipitare「头朝下抛落」构成。

items.en: The verb joins prae- 'before, forth' with caput 'head' (stem capit-). The picture is someone diving forward, head first.
items.cn: 这个动词由 prae-「在前、向前」与 caput「头」（词干 capit-）组成。画面是一个人向前、头朝下地栽下去。

items.en: Alchemical and medical Latin used praecipitatio for a substance settling out of a liquid, and English writers borrowed this technical sense.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中的炼金术与医学用语用 praecipitatio 指物质从液体中沉降出来，英语作者借入了这一技术义。

items.en: Meteorologists applied the same noun to rain and snow falling from clouds, the modern everyday sense.
items.cn: 十七世纪的气象写作者把同一个名词用到从云中落下的雨雪上，形成现代日常义。

items.en: Chemistry standardized precipitation for the formation of a solid, and climate science made it the standard word for measured rainfall and snowfall totals.
items.cn: 十九至二十世纪，化学把 precipitation 固定为固体析出的术语，气候科学则用它作为雨雪总量的标准词。

note.en: Group one holds longer words that share the -pitation shape; group two holds the everyday weather words it covers.
note.cn: 第一组是与该词共享 -pitation 词形的长词；第二组是它所涵盖的日常天气词。

entries.definition: Taking part in an activity. It comes from Latin particeps 'sharing', and the -cip- here is from capere 'to take', a different family.
entries.definitionCN: 参与某项活动。源自拉丁语 particeps「分享」，其中的 -cip- 出自 capere「拿取」，属另一词族。

entries.definition: The act of noticing or understanding something. It comes from percipere 'to seize wholly', not from praecipitare.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉或理解某事的行为。源自 percipere「完全抓住」，并非出自 praecipitare。

entries.definition: The act of getting something ready. The base is parare 'to make ready', so the resemblance is only in length and rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物准备好的行为。词基是 parare「准备」，相似之处只在词长与节奏。

entries.definition: Rain measured over a period; it excludes snow and hail, while precipitation includes every form.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间内测得的雨量；它不包括雪和冰雹，而 precipitation 包含一切形态。

entries.definition: Snow that falls, or its measured amount; it is one member of the precipitation class.
entries.definitionCN: 落下的雪或其测定量；它是降水这一大类中的一种。

entries.definition: The change from vapour to liquid that must happen before precipitation; it names the step, not the fall.
entries.definitionCN: 降水发生前必须完成的水汽变液体；它指这一步，而不是落下。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin pieces, real chemistry terms, no invented stories.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：使用真实的拉丁构件与化学术语，不编故事。

normal.en: pre- 'before' + capit- 'head' + -ation: something that goes head first out of the sky or out of a solution.
normal.cn: pre-「在前」+ capit-「头」+ -ation：从天空或溶液里「头朝下」出来的东西。

normal.en: precipitation and precipitate share one root; precipitation is the process, precipitate is the solid or the verb.
normal.cn: precipitation 与 precipitate 共享一个词根：前者是过程，后者是固体或动词。

normal.en: precipitous 'steep' keeps the same image: a cliff where one false step sends you head first.
normal.cn: precipitous「陡峭的」保留同一意象：在悬崖上一步踏错就会头朝下栽下去。

normal.en: acid precipitation is the technical name behind the everyday term acid rain.
normal.cn: acid precipitation 是日常说法 acid rain（酸雨）背后的技术名称。

normal.en: The gauge phrase precipitation total pairs the event with its number, which is why the noun can mean both.
normal.cn: precipitation total 这一搭配把事件与数字配在一起，这正是该名词能同时指两者的原因。

abstract.en: Abstractly, precipitation is anything that leaves a floating state and goes down: water leaving a cloud, a solid leaving a solution, a crisis leaving the future and landing in the present.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，precipitation 是任何离开悬浮状态而向下落的东西：水离开云，固体离开溶液，危机离开未来而落到眼前。

abstract.en: The direction is always downward, and the agent is always something that can no longer stay suspended.
abstract.cn: 方向永远是向下，主体永远是那个再也悬浮不住的东西。

abstract.en: So the weather sense and the chemistry sense are one geometry: a ceiling gives way, and what was held falls.
abstract.cn: 所以天气义与化学义是同一个几何：顶托不住了，原本被托住的东西就落下来。

examples.en: The station records precipitation every morning at eight.
examples.cn: 该站每天早上八点记录降水量。

examples.en: Calcium carbonate precipitation sealed the cracks in the cave floor.
examples.cn: 碳酸钙沉淀把洞底的裂缝封住了。

examples.en: A sudden precipitation of events left the negotiators no time to consult.
examples.cn: 事态的骤然爆发让谈判者来不及磋商。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「泼湿皮特」：天上泼下水，把皮特浇湿 → precipitation 降水

root: 拉丁语 praecipitatio「头朝下坠落」← praecipitare「抛落」，由 prae-「向前」+ caput「头」构成；与 precipice、precipitous 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one downward motion. Water falls from a cloud, is counted in a gauge, takes frozen forms, then the same motion appears in a beaker as a solid, in public life as a sudden event, and in character as haste.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个向下动作。水从云里落下，被雨量筒计量，呈现冻结形态；随后同一动作出现在烧杯里成为固体，在公共生活中成为突发事件，在性格上成为仓促。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something held up by a ceiling suddenly gives way and falls head first.
core.cn: 核心意象：被一层顶托住的东西忽然失去支撑，头朝下坠落。

branches.en: WHAT FALLS: liquid rain and frozen snow or hail are one class of falling water.
branches.cn: 落下之物：液态的雨与冻结的雪、冰雹都属同一类落下的水。

branches.en: HOW MUCH: a gauge turns the event into millimetres and inches.
branches.cn: 落了多少：雨量筒把事件变成毫米与英寸。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: a dissolved substance leaves the liquid as a solid, and the solid takes the same name.
branches.cn: 化学：溶解的物质离开液体成为固体，这个固体也用同一个名称。

branches.en: HUMAN TIME: an event falls on people too soon, and the person who causes it is judged hasty.
branches.cn: 人的时间：事件过早砸到人身上，促成它的人则被评判为仓促。

branches.en: MECHANISM: meteorology names the whole condensation-and-fall chain.
branches.cn: 机制：气象学用这个词命名凝结到落下的整条链条。

intro.en: The family is built from Latin prae- plus caput. English adds -ation for the process, -ous for the steep version, and -or for an instrument.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁 prae- 加 caput 构成。英语加 -ation 表示过程，加 -ous 表示陡峭，加 -or 表示器具。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries below are the recorded ancestors and relatives of the family; they are listed as Latin, not as modern English words.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁条目是该词族有记录的祖先与亲属；它们按拉丁语列出，而不是现代英语词。

items.meaning: to cause a solid to form; the solid itself; hasty
items.meaningCN: 使固体析出；析出的固体；仓促的
items.example: The reagent precipitates the metal as a salt.
items.exampleCN: 试剂使金属以盐的形式沉淀出来。

items.meaning: extremely steep, like a cliff that drops away
items.meaningCN: 陡峭的，像骤然下落的悬崖（-ous 表示「充满……」）
items.example: A precipitous path led down to the shore.
items.exampleCN: 一条陡峭的小路通向岸边。

items.meaning: a very steep cliff or a dangerous situation
items.example: The goats stood at the edge of the precipice.

items.meaning: a substance that causes another substance to precipitate
items.meaningCN: 沉淀剂（-ant 表示施动者）
items.example: Add the precipitant slowly and stir.
items.exampleCN: 缓慢加入沉淀剂并搅拌。

items.meaning: a device that removes particles from a gas by electrical attraction
items.meaningCN: 静电除尘器；沉淀器（-or 表示器具）
items.example: The electrostatic precipitator catches the fly ash.

items.meaning: a chemical reaction that produces an insoluble solid
items.meaningCN: 沉淀反应（生成不溶固体的化学反应）
items.example: The lab demonstrates a precipitation reaction with silver nitrate.
items.exampleCN: 实验用硝酸银演示一个沉淀反应。

items.meaning: rain or snow made acidic by dissolved pollutants
items.meaningCN: 酸性降水；酸雨（因溶解污染物而呈酸性的雨雪）
items.example: Acid precipitation has damaged the lakes.
items.exampleCN: 酸性降水已经损害了这些湖泊。

items.meaning: the act or factor that causes something to happen or settle
items.meaningCN: 促成……的；正在沉淀的（-ing 分词形式）
items.example: A poor harvest was the precipitating cause of the revolt.
items.exampleCN: 歉收是这场起义的直接诱因。

latinEntries.meaning: to throw down headlong; to hasten

latinEntries.meaningCN: 头朝下的；陡峭的；鲁莽的

definition_zh: 灭绝；消亡；（权利、债务的）消灭；（星光）消光
definition_en: the dying out of a species or the ending of something altogether
core_image: 一排灯原本一盏接一盏亮着，最后一盏也熄掉，整排陷入黑暗
scene: 这里指「灭绝」。 The extinction of the passenger pigeon became a warning for conservationists.
sceneCN: 这里 extinction 指「一个物种彻底消失」（第 1 个义项：某物种的最后个体死亡，种群不再延续）；句意为旅鸽的灭绝成了自然保护者的警钟。图中可辨识物件：空荡的树枝、褪色的鸟形轮廓、标本柜、记录的日期。

pos.zh: 灭绝；消亡；消灭（可数，复数 extinctions）

senses.title: A species dying out completely
senses.definition: the death of the last members of a species, so that it no longer exists
senses.definitionCN: 某物种最后个体死亡，从此不再存在
senses.example: The extinction of the passenger pigeon became a warning for conservationists.
senses.exampleCN: 旅鸽的灭绝成了自然保护者的警钟。
senses.why: extinction is the noun of extinguishing: a flame goes out and nothing of it is left, which is exactly the image used for a species.
senses.whyCN: extinction 是「熄灭」的名词：火苗灭掉后什么也不剩，物种灭绝用的正是这个意象。

senses.title: The process of dying out
senses.definition: the process by which the last members of a group decline and disappear
senses.definitionCN: 某类群最后的成员逐渐减少并消失的过程
senses.example: The extinction of the dodo unfolded over less than a century.
senses.exampleCN: 渡鸦的灭绝在不到一个世纪内展开。
senses.why: the noun names both the endpoint and the road to it, and the process reading is the one used in ecology.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既指终点也指通往终点的路，生态学用的是过程这一读法。

senses.title: Local extinction, or extirpation
senses.titleCN: 局部灭绝：某地消失但别处尚有
senses.definition: the disappearance of a species from one region while it survives elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 某物种在一个地区消失，但在别处仍然存在
senses.example: Wolves faced local extinction in the lowlands but held on in the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 狼在低地遭遇局部灭绝，但在山区存续下来。
senses.why: because a species can vanish locally without vanishing globally, the noun takes a qualifier to mark the smaller scale.
senses.whyCN: 因为物种可以在本地消失而不在全球消失，这个名词需要限定语来标记较小的尺度。

senses.title: A mass extinction
senses.titleCN: 大灭绝：短时间内大量物种消失
senses.definition: an event in which a large share of all species disappears in a short span of geological time
senses.definitionCN: 在地质时间的短促跨度内，大比例物种消失的事件
senses.example: The end-Permian mass extinction removed most marine families.
senses.exampleCN: 二叠纪末大灭绝抹去了大多数海洋科。
senses.why: mass marks the scale, and extinction supplies the verb-derived idea of everything going out at once.
senses.whyCN: mass 标记规模，extinction 提供「一齐熄灭」的动词意象。

senses.title: A language or culture dying out
senses.definition: the disappearance of a language or way of life when its last speakers or practitioners die
senses.definitionCN: 语言或生活方式因最后使用者的离世而消失
senses.example: Linguists race to record languages facing extinction.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学家争相记录面临消亡的语言。
senses.why: the metaphor transfers the biological sense to anything whose carriers can die out, which is why languages are said to go extinct.
senses.whyCN: 这一隐喻把生物学含义移到任何「承载者会消亡」的事物上，因此语言也被说成灭绝。

senses.title: Dimming of starlight by dust
senses.titleCN: 天文学义：星际尘埃导致的星光消光
senses.definition: the absorption and scattering of starlight by interstellar matter
senses.definitionCN: 星际物质对星光的吸收与散射
senses.example: Interstellar dust causes the extinction of light from distant stars.
senses.exampleCN: 星际尘埃使远处恒星的光发生消光。
senses.why: astronomers borrowed the word because light is literally put out along the way, in the same sense as a flame.
senses.whyCN: 天文学家借用这个词，因为光确实在途中被「熄灭」，与火苗同理。

senses.title: A right or debt extinguished
senses.titleCN: 法律义：权利或债务的消灭
senses.definition: the ending of a legal right or obligation, as when a debt is paid off
senses.definitionCN: 某项法律权利或义务的终止，如债务清偿后消灭
senses.example: Payment produced the extinction of the debt.
senses.exampleCN: 付款使该债务归于消灭。
senses.why: law uses the word for anything that ceases to exist in the eyes of the law, keeping the core idea of being put out.
senses.whyCN: 法律用它指在法律眼中不复存在的事物，保留了「被熄灭」的核心。

senses.title: A conditioned response dying out
senses.titleCN: 行为心理学义：条件反应消退
senses.definition: the weakening and disappearance of a learned response when it is no longer reinforced
senses.definitionCN: 学习得来的反应因不再被强化而减弱并消失
senses.example: Extinction of the conditioned response followed repeated non-reinforcement.
senses.exampleCN: 在反复不予强化之后，条件反应出现了消退。
senses.why: psychology borrowed it for a response that fades away, treating the behaviour as the flame that goes out.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借它指逐渐消失的反应，把行为当作被熄灭的火。

intro.en: Extinction comes from Latin exstinctio, built on exstinguere 'to quench, put out', from ex- 'out' and stinguere 'to prick, quench'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: extinction 来自拉丁 exstinctio，基于 exstinguere「熄灭、扑灭」，由 ex-「向外」与 stinguere「刺、熄灭」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stinguere meant 'to prick or quench'. its deeper origin is uncertain; a link to a root meaning 'to stick, prick' is a reconstruction rather than a demonstrated fact.
items.cn: stinguere 意为「刺、熄灭」。其更深来源不确定；把它连到表示「刺、扎」的词根只是重构，并非已证事实。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus stinguere gave exstinguere 'to put out, quench, destroy', used of fires, lights and, figuratively, of families.
items.cn: ex-「向外」加 stinguere 得 exstinguere「扑灭、熄灭、毁掉」，用于火与光，也比喻家族断绝。

items.en: The noun exstinctio named a quenching or a putting out; English took it as extinction in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 exstinctio 指熄灭或扑灭；英语于 15 世纪以 extinction 吸收。

items.en: The sense of a species dying out is recorded from the nineteenth century, as naturalists assembled the fossil record of vanished forms.
items.cn: 物种灭绝的意思在 19 世纪有记录，当时博物学家整理已消失类型的化石记录。

items.en: The twentieth century added the astronomical sense of light extinction and the psychological sense of response extinction.
items.cn: 20 世纪又增添了天文学的「消光」义与心理学的「反应消退」义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates and deeper root): the exact first citation of the biological sense is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of stinguere remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：生物义的最早书证没有确定；stinguere 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same stinguere stock that look alike; group two holds words for things ending, which differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 stinguere 词干、形似的词；第二组表示「终结」，范围不同。

entries.definition: The state of having died out; extinction is the event or process that produces that state.
entries.definitionCN: 指已灭绝的状态；extinction 是造成该状态的事件或过程。

entries.definition: To put out a fire or light, or to wipe out a right; the noun extinction is its result.
entries.definitionCN: 扑灭火或光，或使权利消灭；名词 extinction 是其结果。

entries.definition: Dis- 'apart' plus stinguere: to mark things apart, hence to tell them apart. It has nothing to do with dying out.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「分开」加 stinguere：把事物区分开，因此指辨别。与灭绝无关。

entries.definition: In- 'in' plus stinguere, literally 'pricked on': an inborn drive. The same root, a very different path.
entries.definitionCN: in-「在内」加 stinguere，字面为「被内在刺动」：天生的驱力。同根而走向完全不同。

entries.definition: The removal of a species from one area while it survives elsewhere; extinction means the species is gone everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物种在一地被清除而别处仍存；extinction 指该物种处处不见。

entries.definition: A sharp local loss of many individuals; it need not end the species.
entries.definitionCN: 指一地大量个体骤然死亡；未必导致物种终结。

entries.definition: A broad word for removing something, from rivals to waste; it lacks the biological finality of extinction.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指去除，从对手到废物；不含 extinction 那种生物学上的终结性。

entries.definition: The fact of no longer being seen; a species may disappear from a survey and still return.
entries.definitionCN: 指不再被看见；物种可能从调查中消失却仍然回来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + stinguere 'quench': the flame is put right out.
normal.cn: ex-「向外」+ stinguere「熄灭」：火被彻底弄灭。

normal.en: The family runs extinction, extinct, extinguish, extinguisher, extinguishment.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 extinction、extinct、extinguish、extinguisher、extinguishment。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: mass extinction, extinction event, brink of extinction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出规模：大灭绝、灭绝事件、灭绝边缘。

normal.en: The same root shows in distinguish and instinct, both with different prefixes.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 distinguish 与 instinct 中，前缀都不同。

normal.en: Ecology counts local extinction separately from global extinction.
normal.cn: 生态学把局部灭绝与全球灭绝分开计数。

abstract.en: Picture the last candle in a row going out, and the room going dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一排蜡烛的最后一支熄灭，房间陷入黑暗。

abstract.en: Picture a language with one elderly speaker left, and then none.
abstract.cn: 想象一门语言只剩一位老人会说，然后一个也不剩。

abstract.en: Picture a star whose light is eaten by dust before it reaches a telescope.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗星的光在到达望远镜前被尘埃吃掉。

examples.en: Habitat loss is the leading cause of extinction today.
examples.cn: 生境丧失是当今灭绝的首要原因。

examples.en: The extinction rate is now far above the fossil background.
examples.cn: 当前的灭绝速率远高于化石记录的背景值。

examples.en: The debt's extinction must be recorded in the ledger.
examples.cn: 债务的消灭必须记入账簿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）+ tinct（熄灭）」——火苗彻底熄掉，什么也不剩 → 灭绝、消亡

root: 拉丁 exstinctio「熄灭」来自 exstinguere（ex-「向外」+ stinguere「刺、熄灭」）；stinguere 更深来源不确定，与 distinguish、instinct 同根不同前缀。英语 extinction。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: something is put out, and the putting-out is then read as a species, a process, a local loss, a mass event, a language, a beam of starlight, a legal right and a learned response.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个意象展开：某物被熄灭，这个「熄灭」再被读成物种、过程、局部丧失、大规模事件、语言、一束星光、法律权利与习得反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last flame of a row is put out and the row goes dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排火的最后一支被弄灭，整排陷入黑暗。

branches.en: SPECIES AND PROCESS: either the final state or the road that leads to it.
branches.cn: 物种与过程：或指终局状态，或指通向终局的路。

branches.en: SCALE MARKERS: a loss can be local, or vast enough to count as mass.
branches.cn: 尺度标记：丧失可以是局部的，也可以大到算作大灭绝。

branches.en: CARRIERS DIE OUT: languages and customs are treated as if they had last speakers.
branches.cn: 承载者消亡：语言与习俗被当作有「最后使用者」的事物。

branches.en: LIGHT PUT OUT: dust quenches starlight along the path.
branches.cn: 光被熄灭：尘埃在途中把星光弄灭。

branches.en: OTHER ENDINGS: rights and learned responses also cease to exist.
branches.cn: 其他终结：权利与习得反应同样不复存在。

intro.en: Extinction is a Latin noun of prefix plus root; ex- carries the sense of 'out', and the root also builds extinguish, distinguish and instinct.
intro.cn: extinction 是前缀加词根的拉丁名词；ex- 带「向外」的意思，同一词根还构成 extinguish、distinguish 与 instinct。

latinIntro.en: Latin exstinguere gives extinction, extinct and extinguish; dis- and in- versions of the same root give distinguish and instinct.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 exstinguere 衍生 extinction、extinct 与 extinguish；同一词根的 dis- 与 in- 版本给出 distinguish 与 instinct。

items.example: The prefix marks the flame being driven out.
The root supplies the quenching image.
Mass extinction removed most marine families.
items.exampleCN: 大灭绝抹去了大多数海洋科。

items.example: Crews extinguished the fire within an hour.
items.exampleCN: 消防队在小时内扑灭了火。

items.meaning: a device for putting out fires
items.example: The extinguisher sits by the door.

items.meaning: to mark apart; to tell apart
items.example: The stripes distinguish the two species.
items.exampleCN: 条纹把这两个物种区分开。

items.example: The bird finds the route by instinct.
items.exampleCN: 这种鸟靠本能找到路线。

items.meaning: tending to put out or end
items.example: The extinctive clause ended the easement.
items.exampleCN: 那条消灭条款终止了地役权。

latinEntries.structure: exstinctus, exstincta, exstinctum (past participle used as adjective)

definition_zh: 技术的；技术上的；由技术引起的；技术先进的
definition_en: relating to technology, or brought about by machines, methods and applied knowledge
core_image: 车间里机械臂沿轨道移动，传感器把每一次位移变成屏幕上的数据点
scene: 车间里机械臂按程序移动，工程师把新装的传感器称为这一轮升级的关键。 Technological change reached the workshop long before the office noticed.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「由技术发展带来的变化」（第 3 个义项：由机器、方法与应用知识引起的变化）；句意为技术变化早在办公室察觉之前就到了车间。图中可辨识物件：机械臂、轨道、传感器、数据屏。

pos.zh: 技术的；与技术有关的
由技术引起的；技术先进的

senses.title: Relating to technology in general
senses.definition: connected with the tools, methods and applied knowledge a society uses
senses.definitionCN: 与社会所使用的工具、方法及应用知识有关
senses.example: Technological change reached the workshop long before the office noticed.
senses.exampleCN: 技术变化早在办公室察觉之前就到了车间。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun for the study of crafts to any subject it describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把表示「技艺之学」的名词挂到它所描述的对象上。

senses.title: Advanced in equipment or method
senses.titleCN: 技术先进的；装备水平高的
senses.definition: equipped with or relying on a high level of machinery and method
senses.definitionCN: 装备或依赖高水平机器与方法的
senses.example: Their newest line is highly technological, with sensors at every station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们最新的生产线技术含量很高，每个工位都有传感器。
senses.why: A plant that depends on many devices can be described by the adjective, so 'related to technology' shades into 'full of it'.
senses.whyCN: 依赖大量装置的工厂可以用这个形容词描述，于是「与技术有关」滑向「技术密集」。

senses.title: Caused by technology
senses.definition: brought about by machines or new methods rather than by nature or policy
senses.definitionCN: 由机器或新方法而非自然或政策造成的
senses.example: Technological unemployment follows when machines replace routine tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 当机器取代常规工作时，就会出现技术性失业。
senses.why: Once the adjective marks a cause, it can label effects that would not exist without the tools.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词标记原因时，它就能给那些离开工具便不会存在的后果贴标签。

senses.title: Pertaining to the limits of equipment
senses.definition: concerning what the available tools and methods can or cannot do
senses.definitionCN: 涉及现有工具与方法能做到或做不到什么
senses.example: The boundary is technological rather than legal.
senses.exampleCN: 这道界限是技术上的，而非法律上的。
senses.why: A limit set by tools is distinct from one set by law, and the adjective separates the two causes.
senses.whyCN: 工具造成的限制与法律造成的限制不同，这个形容词把两种原因分开。

senses.title: Demanding technical skill
senses.definition: requiring specialised method or skill rather than ordinary handling
senses.definitionCN: 需要专门方法或技艺，而非一般操作的
senses.example: Dyeing is the most technological step in the whole process.
senses.exampleCN: 染色是整个流程中技术性最强的一步。
senses.why: Where a step depends on exact methods, it is technological in the older sense of belonging to a craft.
senses.whyCN: 当一道步骤依赖精确方法时，它在「属于一门技艺」的较早意义上就是技术性的。

senses.title: Belonging to technical research
senses.definition: of the branch of work that develops tools and processes, as distinct from pure science
senses.definitionCN: 指开发工具与工艺的那类工作，与纯科学相区别
senses.example: Technological research and pure science answer different questions.
senses.exampleCN: 技术研究与纯科学回答的是不同的问题。
senses.why: Research aimed at making things work is separated from research aimed at understanding, and the adjective marks the first.
senses.whyCN: 以让东西能用为目标的研究，与以理解为目标的研究被区分开，这个形容词标记前者。

senses.title: Treating tools as the driver of history
senses.definition: in social theory, explaining change chiefly by the state of the tools
senses.definitionCN: 在社会理论中，主要以工具状况解释变化
senses.example: A technological view of history makes tools the driver of change.
senses.exampleCN: 一种技术论的历史观把工具当作变化的驱动力。
senses.why: When the adjective modifies a view rather than a thing, it claims that technology causes history.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词修饰的是一种观点而非物件时，它主张技术造成了历史。

senses.title: Pertaining to craft skill in restoration
senses.definition: concerning the manual and material knowledge needed to preserve or repair objects
senses.definitionCN: 涉及保存或修复物件所需的手工与材料知识
senses.example: The restoration needed technological skill as much as taste.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修复既需要品味，也同样需要工艺技术。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is craft, so repair work that depends on material knowledge is technological too.
senses.whyCN: 词根最古老的意思是技艺，因此依赖材料知识的修复工作同样属于技术层面。

intro.en: Technological joins a Greek noun for craft to a Greek suffix for study, and only in the modern period did it come to mean machines. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词把一个希腊语中表示「技艺」的名词连到表示「学问」的后缀上，直到近代才用来指机器。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tekhne meant 'craft, skill, art', the knowledge of how to make something. Its earlier origin is reconstructed from a root often glossed 'to weave or fabricate', so source uncertain at that depth.
items.cn: tekhne 意为「技艺、技能、手艺」，即知道如何制作某物。其更早来源由常被解释为「编织、制作」的词根重构而来，故更深一层来源不确定。

items.en: The suffix -logia meant 'the study or account of', from logos 'word, reason, reckoning'.
items.cn: 后缀 -logia 意为「对……的论述或研究」，出自 logos「言词、理性、计算」。

items.en: Tekhnologia in Greek meant a systematic treatment of an art, not the art of machines.
items.cn: 希腊语 tekhno-logia 指对某门技艺的系统论述，而不是机器之术。

items.en: English technology first named a discourse on an art; the sense of practical arts and then machines developed later.
items.cn: 这个词最初指对一门技艺的论述；实用技艺义、再到机器义是后来发展的。

items.en: The adjective appeared in the nineteenth century, when industry began to be described in terms of applied knowledge and machinery.
items.cn: 这个形容词出现于十九世纪，当时人们开始用应用知识与机械来描述工业。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek root with different jobs, which are constantly confused; group two holds adjectives for advanced or machine-based work.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊词根但分工不同的词，最易混淆；第二组是表示先进或机器化的形容词。

entries.tag: of a craft or a detail
entries.definition: Belonging to a particular craft or to the mechanical details of a subject; a technical fault is a small mechanical one.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某一门技艺或某一主题的机械细节；技术故障指小的机械问题。

entries.definition: A way of doing something skilfully; it is the craft itself, not the adjective of relation.
entries.definitionCN: 熟练做某事的方法，是手艺本身，而非表示关系的形容词。

entries.definition: The body of tools, methods and knowledge; the adjective describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 工具、方法与知识的整体，形容词描述属于它的东西。

entries.definition: The adverb form, used of processes and states rather than of things.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，多用于过程与状态，而非物件。

entries.definition: Far along in development; it praises the level without naming the tools.
entries.definitionCN: 发展程度高，赞的是水平，不点明所用工具。

entries.definition: Working through numerical signals; it is narrower than technological and names a family of devices.
entries.definitionCN: 通过数字信号工作，比「技术的」窄，指一族装置。

entries.definition: Belonging to manufacturing on a large scale; a technological change need not be industrial.
entries.definitionCN: 属于大规模制造，技术变化未必是工业的。

entries.definition: Driven by physical parts; it covers only one part of what the adjective covers.
entries.definitionCN: 由物理部件驱动，只覆盖这个形容词所指的一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A Greek noun for craft plus a suffix for systematic study: the adjective describes whatever belongs to that study.
normal.cn: 希腊语「技艺」名词加表示系统学问的后缀：这个形容词描述属于这门学问的一切。

normal.en: The family runs technology, technologist, technically, technique and the adverb in -ly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括技术、技术专家、技术性地、技巧，以及加副后缀的形式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the theme: change, development, innovation, advance, progress, breakthrough.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出主题：技术变革、技术发展、技术创新、技术进步、技术进展、技术突破。

normal.en: The root meant craft long before it meant machines, which is why a restorer's skill is also called technological.
normal.cn: 词根在指机器之前很久就指技艺，因此修复师的手艺也算技术层面。

normal.en: Keep the pair apart: technical points to a detail or a craft, technological points to the system of tools.
normal.cn: 要分清这一对：一个指向细节或某门手艺，另一个指向工具系统。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that once held a chisel and now holds a controller.
abstract.cn: 想象同一只手，从前握着凿子，如今握着控制器。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where every movement leaves a trace on a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一间车间，每个动作都在屏幕上留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a timetable that changes because a machine changed, not because anyone voted.
abstract.cn: 想象一份时刻表因一台机器改变而改变，而不是因为有人投票。

examples.en: The gap between rich and poor regions is partly technological.
examples.cn: 富区与穷区之间的差距有一部分是技术上的。

examples.en: Technological advances in cooling made the desert farm possible.
examples.cn: 制冷技术的进步使沙漠农场成为可能。

examples.en: The report treats technological and legal barriers separately.
examples.cn: 报告把技术障碍与法律障碍分开处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「techno（技艺）+ logical（学问的）」——关于技艺之学的 → 技术的、技术引起的

root: 希腊语「技艺」名词加表示「系统学问」的后缀，再加形容词后缀；该名词的更早来源属重构形式，通常解释为「编织、制作」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective: it points at tools in general, then at a high level of them, then at effects they cause, at limits they set, at skill they demand, at the research that improves them, at a theory that makes them the cause of history, and finally at the old craft sense of skilled hands.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形容词展开：先泛指工具，再指工具水平高，接着指工具造成的后果、设定的限制、要求的技艺、改进它们的研究、把它们当作历史动因的理论，最后回到「巧手之艺」的古老含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mechanical arm moving along a rail while a sensor turns each movement into a point of light on a screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：机械臂沿轨道移动，传感器把每一次位移变成屏幕上的一个光点。

branches.en: TOOLS IN GENERAL AND TOOLS IN PLENTY: the broad relation and the high level differ only in degree.
branches.cn: 泛指工具与工具密集：宽泛的关系与高水平只差程度。

branches.en: TOOLS AS CAUSE: an effect on employment and a theory of history both make the tool the reason.
branches.cn: 工具作为原因：对就业的影响与对历史的解释，都把工具当作理由。

branches.en: TOOLS AS LIMIT AND AS DEMAND: what equipment cannot do and what skill it requires are two faces of one constraint.
branches.cn: 工具作为限制与要求：设备做不到的事与它要求的技艺，是同一约束的两面。

branches.en: IMPROVING THE TOOLS: research aimed at better tools is the engine of the whole chain.
branches.cn: 改进工具：以更好的工具为目标的研究，是整条链条的发动机。

branches.en: THE OLD CRAFT: restoration returns the word to skilled hands and materials.
branches.cn: 古老的技艺：修复工作把这个词带回巧手与材料。

intro.en: Technological is built from a Greek noun of craft, a Greek suffix of study and a Latin-shaped adjective ending, so three layers meet in one word.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个希腊语「技艺」名词、一个表示「学问」的希腊后缀和一个拉丁形态的形容词词尾构成，因此三层来源汇于一词。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin technologia carried the Greek compound into learned writing, and Late Latin technicus supplied the adjective of craft.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把这一希腊复合词带入学术写作，晚期拉丁语则提供了表示「技艺的」形容词。

items.example: The root names the knowledge of how to make.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指「知道怎么做」的知识。

items.example: The suffix makes a systematic account of the craft.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀使技艺成为系统论述的对象。

items.example: The combining form allows the noun to be joined to suffixes.
items.exampleCN: 这个组合形式使名词能接后缀。

items.meaning: a systematic treatment of an art
items.meaningCN: 对某门技艺的系统论述
items.example: The medieval noun still meant discourse, not machinery.
items.exampleCN: 这个中世纪名词仍指论述，而非机械。

items.meaning: the body of tools and methods
items.example: The modern noun narrowed to practical arts and then to machines.
items.exampleCN: 现代名词先收窄为实用技艺，再收窄为机器。

items.example: The ending makes the adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成表示关系的形容词。

items.example: The adjective appeared when industry was described as applied knowledge.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词出现于人们用应用知识描述工业之时。

items.example: The adverb marks the point of view rather than the thing.

definition_en: the loss of water vapour from plants, mainly through the stomata

scene: 正午的玉米地叶片卷起，根吸上来的水大部分并没有留在植株里。 Most of that water leaves the field by transpiration.
sceneCN: 这里 transpiration 指「植物经气孔散失水汽的过程」（第 1 个义项：作为整株植物的失水过程）；句意：那些水大部分以蒸腾作用离开了这块田。

pos.zh: 蒸腾作用（植物失水，不可数）
散发；蒸发（一般意义的水汽散出）

senses.title: Water loss from plants
senses.titleCN: 植物失水：水从叶面变成水汽
senses.definition: the loss of water vapour from a plant, mainly through its stomata
senses.definitionCN: 植物主要经气孔散失水汽的过程
senses.example: Most of that water leaves the field by transpiration.
senses.exampleCN: 那些水大部分以蒸腾作用离开了这块田。
senses.why: The plant is a wick: water enters at the roots, moves up, and leaves as vapour at the leaves.
senses.whyCN: 植物就是一根烛芯：水从根进、往上走，最后在叶片以水汽离开。

senses.title: The pull
senses.titleCN: 蒸腾拉力：水柱被向上拽
senses.definition: the tension that the loss of vapour creates, drawing water up the plant
senses.definitionCN: 水汽散失造成的拉力，把水沿植物体向上拉
senses.example: Transpiration pull lifts water to the tallest leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸腾拉力把水送到最高的叶片。
senses.why: Every litre that leaves the leaf pulls another litre up behind it, so loss and lift are one mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 每从叶片走掉一升水，就往上拽进另一升，于是失水与提升是同一套机制。

senses.title: Rate
senses.titleCN: 速率：单位时间失去多少水
senses.definition: the measured rate at which a plant loses water vapour
senses.definitionCN: 单位时间内散失水汽的速率
senses.example: They measured transpiration with a potometer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用蒸腾计测蒸腾速率。
senses.why: Once the process is named, instruments can give it a number, and the word comes to mean that number.
senses.whyCN: 过程一旦有了名字，仪器就能给它一个数，这个词也随之指那个数。

senses.title: Cooling
senses.definition: the cooling of a leaf that the evaporation of water produces
senses.definitionCN: 水分蒸发给叶片带来的降温
senses.example: Transpiration keeps the leaf below air temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸腾让叶温低于气温。
senses.why: Evaporation takes heat with it, so the same loss that costs water also saves the leaf from overheating.
senses.whyCN: 蒸发会带走热量，于是这份失水在耗水的同时，也让叶片免于过热。

senses.title: Stomatal control
senses.titleCN: 气孔调控：开合决定失水快慢
senses.definition: the regulation of water loss by the opening and closing of the stomata
senses.definitionCN: 气孔开合对失水快慢的调控
senses.example: Transpiration stops when the stomata close at midday.
senses.exampleCN: 正午气孔关闭时，蒸腾就停止了。
senses.why: The pores are the tap, and the word covers whatever flow the tap allows.
senses.whyCN: 气孔是龙头，这个词覆盖龙头允许的那股流量。

senses.title: Water-use ratio
senses.titleCN: 蒸腾比：造一克干物质要用多少水
senses.definition: the ratio of water lost to dry matter gained
senses.definitionCN: 失水量与所得干物质之比
senses.example: A low transpiration ratio marks a thrifty crop.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸腾比低说明这种作物省水。
senses.why: Farmers compare outputs, so the process becomes a ratio of cost to yield.
senses.whyCN: 农人要比较产出，于是这个过程变成一个成本与产量的比值。

senses.title: General vapor release
senses.titleCN: 一般散发：任何表面散出水汽
senses.definition: the release of water vapour from any surface, not only from plants
senses.definitionCN: 任何表面散出水汽，不限于植物
senses.example: Transpiration from the wet soil continued all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 湿土散出的水汽持续了一下午。
senses.why: The word began as a general term for giving off vapour, and the botanical sense narrowed one part of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初泛指散出水汽，植物义只是把其中一部分收窄了。

senses.title: Sweat and exhalation
senses.titleCN: 人体散发：出汗与呼出水汽
senses.definition: the giving off of moisture through the skin or the breath, an older medical use
senses.definitionCN: 经皮肤或呼吸散出水分，属较早的医学用法
senses.example: Old medical texts speak of transpiration through the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的医学文献说到经皮肤的散发。
senses.why: Before it belonged to botany, the word described the body's own invisible moisture, and medicine kept that sense.
senses.whyCN: 在归植物学之前，这个词描述身体自己看不见的水分，医学保留了这层意思。

senses.title: Vapour flux in the water cycle
senses.titleCN: 水汽通量：区域尺度上的失水
senses.definition: the flux of water vapour from a region, summed over its vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 某一区域植被总体散出的水汽通量
senses.example: Transpiration returns a large share of rainfall to the air.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸腾把降水的很大一部分送回空中。
senses.why: Scale the wick from one plant to a catchment and the word becomes a term in the water budget.
senses.whyCN: 把这根烛芯从一株植物放大到一个集水区，这个词就成了水量收支里的一个项。

intro.en: Transpiration joins Latin trans- 'across' to spirare 'to breathe', literally 'a breathing through'.
intro.cn: transpiration 把拉丁 trans-「穿过」与 spirare「呼吸」连起来，字面是「透过去呼吸」。

items.en: Latin spirare meant 'to breathe, to blow', and it also gives spirit, inspire and expire.
items.cn: 拉丁 spirare 意为「呼吸、吹」，它也是 spirit、inspire、expire 的来源。

items.en: Transpirare meant 'to breathe through, to emit vapour', built with the prefix trans- 'across, through'.
items.cn: transpirare 意为「透过去呼吸、散出水汽」，由前缀 trans-「穿过」构成。

items.en: English adopted the noun in the seventeenth century for the giving off of invisible moisture, including from the body.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，指散出看不见的水分，包括身体散出的。

items.en: Nineteenth-century plant physiology narrowed the word to water loss through the stomata, the sense that now dominates.
items.cn: 十九世纪的植物生理学把这个词收窄为经气孔失水，这一义项如今占主导。

items.en: Twentieth-century hydrology extended it again, to vapour fluxes summed over whole regions.
items.cn: 二十世纪的水文学又把它扩展为整个区域的水汽通量。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the Latin roots are certain, but the first English use is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：拉丁词根确定，但英语首次使用的年代只有约数。

note.en: Group one separates the same-root breathing words from the one that means sweat; group two holds the water-loss terms it is confused with.
note.cn: 第一组区分同源的「呼吸」词与表示出汗的那个词；第二组列出常被混淆的失水术语。

entries.definitionCN: 汁液或液体从伤口或表面缓慢渗出。

entries.definitionCN: 土壤蒸发与植物蒸腾相加的总量。

normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用拉丁部件与真实生理过程，不编顺口溜。

normal.cn: trans-「穿过」加 spirare「呼吸」：透过叶片呼吸。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one current: water leaves the leaf, pulls more up behind it, is measured, cools the leaf, is controlled by the pores, becomes a farming ratio, widens to any surface, widens further to the body, and finally to a region's water budget.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一股水流展开：水离开叶片、把后面的水往上拽、被测量、给叶片降温、受气孔控制、变成农业比值，再扩到任何表面、扩到身体，最后扩到一个区域的水量收支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wick that carries water from the root to the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根把水从根送到空气里的烛芯。

branches.en: LOSS: the word first names the water leaving the plant.
branches.cn: 失去：这个词首先命名离开植物的水。

branches.en: TWO EFFECTS: the same loss lifts water and takes heat away.
branches.cn: 两个效果：同一份失水既提水又带走热。

branches.en: NUMBERS: rate and ratio turn the process into a quantity.
branches.cn: 数字：速率与比值把过程变成量。

branches.en: VALVE: the pores decide how fast the loss runs.
branches.cn: 阀门：气孔决定失水跑多快。

branches.en: WIDER: any surface, the body, a whole catchment.
branches.cn: 更广：任何表面、身体、整个集水区。
