senses.definitionCN: 描述通过反复接触使一项与另一项建立联结的学习
senses.example: Associative learning explains why the bell alone came to calm the dog.
senses.exampleCN: 联想学习解释了为什么单靠铃声就能让狗安静下来。
senses.why: Learning by pairing is the mental link put to work: one item comes to stand for another.
senses.whyCN: 由配对进行的学习，就是把心理联结投入使用：一项开始代表另一项。

senses.title: Loose, free-flowing linkage
senses.definition: describing writing or speech that moves by resemblance and memory rather than by argument
senses.definitionCN: 描述写作或言谈靠相似与记忆推进，而非靠论证
senses.example: The essay proceeds by associative jumps rather than by steps.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章靠联想跳跃推进，而不是一步一步来。
senses.why: When links are not checked, they become a style: the adjective turns from a description of memory into a description of method.
senses.whyCN: 当联结不被检验，它就成了一种风格：这个形容词从描述记忆转为描述方法。

senses.title: Of lookup by content rather than address
senses.titleCN: 按内容而非按地址查找的
senses.definition: describing a store that returns a record by matching its content instead of by a fixed location
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种存储：按内容匹配取回记录，而不是按固定位置取回
senses.example: An associative memory returns the record that best matches the key.
senses.exampleCN: 相联存储器返回与检索键最匹配的那条记录。
senses.why: Storage addressed by content keeps the mental idea of likeness, applied to records rather than to ideas.
senses.whyCN: 按内容寻址的存储保留了「相似」这一心理想法，只是把记录代替了念头。

senses.title: Of a body based on voluntary membership
senses.definition: describing organizations or activity built on people joining freely rather than on kinship or decree
senses.definitionCN: 描述靠人们自愿加入、而非靠血缘或命令建立的组织或活动
senses.example: Associative clubs pooled their dues to rent a hall.
senses.exampleCN: 各社团把会费凑起来租下礼堂。
senses.why: Here the Latin noun's social sense returns as an adjective: what is built out of joining.
senses.whyCN: 此处拉丁名词的社会义回到形容词上：凡是由「加入」构成的东西。

senses.title: Of word links that share a context
senses.titleCN: 指共享语境的词间关系
senses.definition: describing relations between words that may replace one another in a context, as against those that combine in sequence
senses.definitionCN: 描述可在同一语境中互相替换的词之间的关系，与按顺序组合的关系相对
senses.example: Associative relations group salt with pepper rather than with sprinkle.
senses.exampleCN: 联想关系把盐与胡椒归在一起，而不是把盐与「撒」这个动作归在一起。
senses.why: Linguistics borrowed the psychological term for the links stored in the mind alongside grammar.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借用了这个心理学术语，指与语法并存、存放在心里的那些联结。

senses.title: Linked by resemblance, not by cause
senses.titleCN: 靠相似而非因果相连的
senses.definition: describing connections made because things look or feel alike rather than because one produced the other
senses.definitionCN: 描述因外观或感觉相似、而非因因果相生而形成的连接
senses.example: The film works through associative images rather than through argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片靠意象的相似牵连起作用，而不是靠论证。
senses.why: When no proof joins them, resemblance alone remains, and the adjective describes that weaker link.
senses.whyCN: 当没有证明把两者连起，只剩相似，这个形容词便描述那种更弱的联结。

intro.en: Associative is associate plus the Latin adjective suffix -ivus 'tending to'. Associate comes from Latin associare 'to unite with'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: associative 是 associate 加拉丁形容词词尾（意为「倾向于……」）构成；associate 出自拉丁 associare「与……联合」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link sometimes proposed to a verb of following is a hypothesis.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人提出它与一个表「跟随」的动词有关，那只是假说。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus sociare 'to join' produced associare 'to unite with', the verb behind the whole English family.
items.cn: 表「朝向」的前缀加 sociare「结伴」构成 associare「与……联合」，是整个英语词族背后的动词。

items.en: The suffix -ivus formed adjectives meaning 'tending to, serving to', and it reached English through French as -ive.
items.cn: 拉丁词尾 -ivus 构成意为「倾向于、用于」的形容词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Associative is recorded in English from the seventeenth century in the philosophy of ideas; the mathematical rule of grouping is named in the nineteenth century, and the psychological and computing uses follow in the twentieth.
items.cn: associative 在十七世纪已见于英语的观念哲学；指分组规则的数学用法在十九世纪得名，心理学与计算技术的用法随后于二十世纪出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact first citation is fixed for the adjective, and the pre-Latin source of socius remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这个形容词没有确切的最早书证；socius 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same Latin verb; group two holds adjectives that also describe how things are linked.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个拉丁动词的各词形；第二组是同样描述「如何相连」的形容词。

entries.definition: Names the link or the body of members; the adjective names the property of working by such links.
entries.definitionCN: 指那条联结或成员团体；形容词则指「以这种联结运作」的性质。

entries.definition: The verb for linking and the noun for a partner; it never carries the mathematical sense of grouping.
entries.definitionCN: 指联结的动词与同伴的名词；它从未带上数学分组义。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something by association, as in thinking associatively; the adjective modifies the thing, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指以联想方式做某事的副词，如「以联想方式思考」；形容词修饰事物，而非动作。

entries.definition: Describes separation rather than joining, as in a dissociative disorder; it is built with a prefix of apartness.
entries.definitionCN: 描述分离而非联结，如解离性障碍；它由表「分开」的前缀构成。

entries.definition: The everyday adjective for anything joined, by wire, by road or by logic; it does not say how the joining is made.
entries.definitionCN: 指被连起来的任何东西，靠电线、道路或逻辑；不说明联结如何形成。

entries.definition: Describing what concerns relations between things, often in databases or grammar; it is broader and more technical than associative.
entries.definitionCN: 描述涉及事物之间关系者，常见于数据库或语法；比 associative 更宽泛也更技术化。

entries.definition: Describing two things that regularly occur together by rule, as in correlative conjunctions; the pairing is grammatical, not mental.
entries.definitionCN: 描述按规则经常同时出现的两项，如关联连词；这种配对是语法性的，而非心理性的。

entries.definition: Describing a device deliberately built to fix something in memory; it may use associations, but its purpose is recall.
entries.definitionCN: 描述为把某物钉在记忆中而特意造出的手段；它可以用联想，但目的是记住。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin suffix -ivus means 'tending to': associative is 'tending to link'.
normal.cn: 拉丁词尾意为「倾向于」：associative 就是「倾向于联结的」。

normal.en: The family runs associate, association, associatively and associativity, all from one verb of joining.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 associate、association、associatively、associativity，全出同一个表「联合」的动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: associative learning in psychology, associative memory in computing, the associative property in algebra.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各领域：心理学的联想学习、计算技术的相联存储、代数的结合律。

normal.en: The mathematical sense is a rule about brackets: change the grouping, keep the answer.
normal.cn: 数学义是一条关于括号的规则：改分组，不改答案。

normal.en: The noun keeps the social sense, so association can still mean a club, while the adjective rarely does.
normal.cn: 名词保留社会义，因此 association 仍可指社团，而形容词很少这样用。

abstract.en: Picture three boxes stacked in any order that still makes one tower.
abstract.cn: 想象三只箱子无论先摞哪两只，堆出来仍是同一座塔。

abstract.en: Picture a page where one word pulls five unrelated words out of the air.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸上，一个词把五个不相干的词从空气里拽出来。

abstract.en: Picture a library shelf that finds a book by what it is about, not by where it sits.
abstract.cn: 想象一排书架，靠书的内容而不是靠位置找到它。

examples.en: Associative memory in the model is addressed by content rather than by location.
examples.cn: 该模型中的联想记忆按内容而非按位置寻址。

examples.en: String concatenation is associative, but subtraction is not.
examples.cn: 字符串拼接满足结合律，而减法不满足。

examples.en: Her associative style of lecturing leaves the connections for the listener to finish.
examples.cn: 她联想式的讲授把联结留给听者自己去补完。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝向」+「结伴」+「倾向于」——倾向于把东西结在一起：心里结是联想，括号里结是结合律。

root: 拉丁 associare「与……联合」加拉丁形容词词尾（意为「倾向于」）；associare = 表「朝向」的前缀 + sociare「结伴」，sociare 出自 socius「同伴」；socius 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a way of linking: ideas calling ideas, brackets that change nothing, pairs learned by exposure, jumps that skip argument, records found by content, bodies built from voluntary joining, words sharing a context, and images joined by resemblance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一种「连起来」的方式：念头带出念头、括号改了结果不变、反复接触学成的配对、跳过论证的跳跃、按内容取回记录、由自愿加入组成的团体、共享语境的词、靠相似相连的意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three boxes stacked in any order into the same tower, beside a page where one word pulls five others out of the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：三只箱子无论先摞哪两只都堆成同一座塔，旁边一页纸上一个词把五个词从空气里拽出来。

branches.en: THE LOOSE CHAIN: a mind that links freely, and a style that lets the links stand unchecked.
branches.cn: 松散的链：自由联结的心，以及任由联结不经检验的风格。

branches.en: THE LEARNED PAIR: repeated exposure welds one item to another.
branches.cn: 学成的配对：反复接触把一项焊在另一项上。

branches.en: THE RULE OF BRACKETS: regrouping changes nothing, which is joining made exact.
branches.cn: 括号的规则：改了分组也不改结果，这是被精确化的「连起来」。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF STORE: records found by content, and people joined by choice.
branches.cn: 两种「库」：按内容取回的记录，与凭自愿加入的人。

branches.en: JOINED BY CONTEXT OR LIKENESS: words that share a setting, and images that resemble each other.
branches.cn: 靠语境或相似相连：共享场景的词，以及彼此相似的意象。

intro.en: The adjective is one root, two prefixes and one suffix: a Latin noun of companionship, a prefix of direction, and a suffix of tendency.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是一个词根、两个前缀与一个后缀的组合：拉丁的「同伴」名词、表方向的前缀、表倾向的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius gives social, society and sociable; sociare with ad- gives associate and association; -ivus gives the tending-to adjectives of English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 衍生 social、society、sociable；sociare 加表方向的前缀衍生 associate 与 association；拉丁词尾 -ivus 构成英语中表「倾向于」的形容词。

items.example: Socius is the person one joins.
items.exampleCN: socius 是与自己结伴的人。

items.example: The verb described two towns sharing one market.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述两座城镇共用一个市集。

items.example: Associare joined one party to another.
items.exampleCN: associare 把一方与另一方连起。

items.example: They associate the tune with summer.
items.exampleCN: 他们把那支曲子与夏天联系起来。
联结性的习惯形成得很快。

items.example: She thinks associatively under time pressure.
items.exampleCN: 她在时间压力下以联想方式思考。
休克之后出现了解离症状。

definition_zh: 石陨石；陨石（旧称，今多用 meteorite）
definition_en: a stony meteorite; an older term for any meteorite, now largely replaced by meteorite in scientific use
core_image: 一块从天上落下来的石头
scene: 博物馆的玻璃柜里躺着一块黑灰色的石块，标签写得很旧。 The aerolite fell in a field two centuries ago.
sceneCN: 这里 aerolite 是「石陨石」（第 1 个义项：以石质为主的陨石）；句意为这块石陨石两个世纪前落在一片田里。核心画面是一块从天上落下来的石头。

pos.zh: 石陨石；陨石

derivatives.zh: 同义异形词，末尾用 -th 而非 -te，义同为「石陨石」
加 -ic 构成，义为「陨石的；与陨石有关的」

senses.title: A stony meteorite
senses.definition: a meteorite composed mainly of silicate rock rather than metal, as opposed to a siderite
senses.definitionCN: 主要由硅酸盐岩石而非金属构成的陨石，与铁陨石相对
senses.example: The aerolite was almost entirely olivine and pyroxene.
senses.exampleCN: 这块石陨石几乎全由橄榄石与辉石构成。
senses.why: Aer means air and lithos means stone, so the word pictures a stone that arrived through the air, and the stony sense is the literal one.
senses.whyCN: aer 意为「空气」，lithos 意为「石头」，所以这个词画的是「穿过空气而来的石头」，石质义正是字面义。

senses.title: Any meteorite, in older usage
senses.definition: in eighteenth and nineteenth century writing, any mass that fell from the sky, whatever its composition
senses.definitionCN: 在十八、十九世纪的文献中，泛指任何自天而降的块体，不论成分
senses.example: Early reports called every such stone an aerolite.
senses.exampleCN: 早期报道把每一块这样的石头都称作 aerolite。
senses.why: Before classification existed, the name covered the whole event of falling, so the word once meant simply a sky-stone of any kind.
senses.whyCN: 在分类学出现之前，这个名字覆盖的是「坠落」这件事本身，所以它一度只表示任何种类的天降之石。

intro.en: Aerolite is a stone named after the sky it came through: air plus stone, written in Greek.
intro.cn: aerolite 是一块以它穿过的天空命名的石头：空气加石头，用希腊语写成。

items.en: Greek aer meant air or the lower atmosphere, the same root as in aerobic.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气、低层大气」，与 aerobic 中的词根相同。

items.en: Greek lithos meant stone, and it gives English lithograph, monolith and Neolithic.
items.cn: 希腊语 lithos 意为「石头」，它给出英语 lithograph、monolith 与 Neolithic。

items.en: French aérolithe was formed in the eighteenth century, when falling stones were still disputed by scholars.
items.cn: 法语 aérolithe 形成于十八世纪，当时学界仍在争论天降石块是否真实。

items.en: English aerolite appeared in the same period and was the standard term for a fallen sky-stone.
items.cn: 英语 aerolite 出现于同一时期，曾是天降石块的标准称呼。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century meteorite displaced aerolite in science, leaving aerolite as a historical and literary word.
items.cn: 自十九世纪后期，meteorite 在科学中取代 aerolite，使 aerolite 成为历史与文学用词。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the stone and sky roots; the near-meaning group lists the modern terms for objects that fall from space.
note.cn: 形近组保留「石」与「天」两个词根；近义组列出天降物体的现代术语。

entries.definition: The same word with -th instead of -te.
entries.definitionCN: 同词异形，末尾为 -th 而非 -te。

entries.definition: A print made from a flat stone surface.
entries.definitionCN: 用平面石版印出的版画。

entries.definition: A balloon or other craft lighter than air.
entries.definitionCN: 气球或其他轻于空气的飞行器。

entries.definition: The current scientific term for a space rock that reaches the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 落到地面的太空岩石的现代科学术语。

entries.definition: A small rocky body still travelling in space.
entries.definitionCN: 仍在太空中运行的小型岩质天体。

entries.definition: An exceptionally bright meteor that often explodes.
entries.definitionCN: 极亮且常发生爆炸的流星。

normalIntro.en: Read aerolite as air-stone: aero is air and lite is lithos, stone.
normalIntro.cn: 把 aerolite 读成「空气之石」：aero 是空气，lite 是 lithos「石头」。

normal.en: Aer plus lite equals air-stone, a stone that came by air.
normal.cn: aer 加 lite 等于空气之石，一块乘空气而来的石头。

normal.en: The lite ending is the same stone as in graphite and chrysolite.
normal.cn: lite 这个词尾与 graphite、chrysolite 中的「石」相同。

normal.en: Aerolite is the old word; meteorite is the one used in papers today.
normal.cn: aerolite 是旧词；meteorite 是今天论文里用的词。

normal.en: Stony aerolite, iron siderite: the old names sorted stones by what they were made of.
normal.cn: 石质叫 aerolite，铁质叫 siderite：旧名按成分分类。

normal.en: Aerolith with -th means exactly the same thing.
normal.cn: 带 -th 的 aerolith 意思完全相同。

abstract.en: Picture a stone that remembers the sky it fell through.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记得自己穿过的那片天空的石头。

abstract.en: Imagine a field at dawn with a black stone still warm in the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明的田野，草里一块仍带余温的黑石。

abstract.en: Think of a museum label older than the science that renamed the object.
abstract.cn: 想象一张比给它改名的那门科学更旧的博物馆标签。

examples.en: The aerolite on display weighs just under two kilograms.
examples.cn: 展出的这块石陨石重不到两公斤。

examples.en: Nineteenth century letters describe the aerolite as a thunderstone.
examples.cn: 十九世纪的书信把这块陨石称作「雷石」。

examples.en: Each aerolite in the drawer was labelled with the date of its fall.
examples.cn: 抽屉里每块陨石都标注了坠落日期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱儿罗来特」——爱（ae）儿（ro）罗（li）来（te），从天上啰啰嗦嗦落下来的那块石头，就是陨石。

root: 希腊语 aer「空气」加 lithos「石头」构成，经法语 aérolithe 进入英语 aerolite，字面即「自空气而来的石头」；十九世纪后期在科学语境中被 meteorite 取代。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same picture at different levels of precision: a stone from the sky, first named by its stony nature and earlier by the mere fact of falling.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一幅画在不同精度下的样子：一块来自天空的石头，先按石质命名，更早则仅按「坠落」这一事实命名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone that arrived through the air
core.cn: 核心意象：一块穿过空气而来的石头

branches.en: The stone named by its silicate makeup.
branches.cn: 按硅酸盐成分命名的石头。

branches.en: The stone named only by its falling.
branches.cn: 仅按坠落这一事实命名的石头。

branches.en: Both keep air plus stone in the spelling.
branches.cn: 两者拼写中都保留空气加石头。

branches.en: The older, wider use before classification.
branches.cn: 分类学之前更宽的旧用法。

branches.en: Both yield to meteorite in modern science.
branches.cn: 两者在现代科学中都让位给 meteorite。

intro.en: Aerolite joins two Greek roots, so its relatives are found by following either the air root or the stone root.
intro.cn: aerolite 连接两个希腊语词根，因此沿着「空气」或「石头」任一词根都能找到它的亲属词。

latinIntro.en: Both roots are Greek; the word reached English through French, and no Latin layer sits between them.
latinIntro.cn: 两个词根都是希腊语；该词经法语进入英语，中间没有拉丁语层。

definition_zh: 保证；把握；自信；安心；保险；质量保证；厚颜
definition_en: a making sure, whether by a promise that removes doubt, a state of certainty, a policy against loss, or too much confidence in oneself
core_image: 一个人把手按在另一个人的肩上，说一声“放心”——把对方心里的不安换成确定
scene: 餐桌上父亲郑重向女儿许诺，办公室里职员递出保单，年轻人走进面试间，仿佛那份工作已属于他。一个词，涵盖三种笃定。 The father's promise to his daughter is an assurance that he will be there.
sceneCN: 这里 assurance 是「保证」（第 1 个义项：旨在使某人安心的郑重承诺）；句意：厨房桌边，父亲向女儿保证他一定会到，这句承诺就是一个保证。场景要点：厨房桌、父亲与女儿、寿险文件、面试门口。

pos.zh: 保证；把握；自信；保险

senses.title: A word given to remove doubt
senses.titleCN: 保证：一句话把疑虑拿掉
senses.definition: a formal or solemn promise meant to give someone confidence
senses.definitionCN: 旨在使某人安心的正式或郑重承诺
senses.example: The company gave an assurance that no jobs would be cut.
senses.exampleCN: 公司保证不会裁员。
senses.why: Late 14c., 'formal or solemn pledge, promise', from Old French asseurance. The noun of -ance names the act of making sure, and a promise is the cheapest instrument for making another mind sure.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪末的“正式或郑重承诺”来自古法语 asseurance。这个 -ance 名词命名“使确定”的动作，而承诺是使另一颗心确定起来最便宜的工具。

senses.title: Certainty in the mind
senses.titleCN: 把握：心里再无怀疑的那种确定
senses.definition: full confidence or certainty that something is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 对某事为真或将会发生的充分信心或确定
senses.example: She spoke with the assurance of someone who had checked every figure.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话时带着一种查过每个数字的人才有的把握。
senses.why: The same late 14c. entry also meant 'certainty, full confidence'. The noun names both the act of making sure and the state of being sure, because -ance can take either side of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 14 世纪末的词条还兼指“确定、充分信心”。这个名词既命名“使确定”的动作，也命名“已确定”的状态，因为 -ance 可以取动词的两面。

senses.title: Carrying yourself as if you cannot fail
senses.titleCN: 自信：走起路来像不会失败
senses.definition: self-confidence, especially in manner or bearing
senses.definitionCN: 自信，尤指态度或举止上的
senses.example: Years of stage work gave her a quiet assurance.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的舞台经历给了她一种安静的自信。
senses.why: The sense 'self-confident' is recorded from the 1590s. Making others sure of you turns inward: the same act now has one's own self as its object.
senses.whyCN: “自信”义记录于 16 世纪 90 年代。使别人对你确定，转向了内部：同一个动作，如今对象成了自己。

senses.title: The calm that follows being told
senses.titleCN: 安心：被告知之后的那口气
senses.definition: a feeling of relief and freedom from worry produced by a promise or explanation
senses.definitionCN: 因承诺或解释而获得的宽慰、免于忧虑之感
senses.example: His assurance that the train would wait let her breathe again.
senses.exampleCN: 他保证火车会等，这才让她重新喘上气来。
senses.why: The verb assure meant 'reassure, give confidence to' from late 14c. Latin securus is literally 'free from care' (se- 'without' + cura 'care'), so assurance names the removal of care rather than the promise that removes it.
senses.whyCN: 动词 assure 从 14 世纪末就意为“使安心、给信心”。拉丁语 securus 字面是“无忧”（se-“无”+ cura“忧虑”），所以 assurance 命名的是忧虑被拿掉，而不是拿掉它的那句承诺。

senses.title: A policy against loss
senses.titleCN: 保险：用一笔钱买下“不会损失”
senses.definition: insurance, especially life insurance (British usage)
senses.definitionCN: 保险，尤指人寿保险（英式用法）
senses.example: He took out a life assurance policy when his first child was born.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个孩子出生时，他买了一份人寿保险。
senses.why: Assurance was the older English word for commercial insurance from the late 16c.; insurance, its en- variant, took over in the 1650s. A premium buys a written promise that loss will be made sure against.
senses.whyCN: 从 16 世纪末起，assurance 就是商业保险较早的英语说法；它的 en- 变体 insurance 在 17 世纪 50 年代接手。保费买下的是一纸承诺：损失会被“确保”抵挡。

senses.title: Quality made certain by process
senses.titleCN: 质量保证：靠流程把质量做成确定
senses.definition: the part of a business that systematically checks that products meet a standard
senses.definitionCN: 企业系统检查产品是否符合标准的部分
senses.example: Quality assurance caught the fault before the parts left the plant.
senses.exampleCN: 质量保证在零件出厂前就查出了缺陷。
senses.why: Twentieth-century industry moved assurance from a spoken promise to a procedure: instead of assuring a customer in words, a firm builds certainty into every step. The abstract noun becomes the name of a department.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的工业把 assurance 从口头承诺变成流程：企业不再用话向客户保证，而是把确定性做进每一道工序。抽象名词于是成了一个部门的名称。

senses.title: A guarantee that something holds
senses.titleCN: 保障：保证某件事站得住
senses.definition: a guarantee that something exists, continues, or is adequate
senses.definitionCN: 对某物存在、持续或足够充分的保证
senses.example: The treaty offers an assurance of water supply to the lower valley.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约为下游河谷提供了供水保障。
senses.why: Here assurance is followed by of rather than that: the noun names the thing made certain, not the sentence spoken. It is the same 'making sure', shifted from a hearer's mind to a fact in the world.
senses.whyCN: 这里 assurance 后接 of 而不是 that：名词命名的是被确保的那件事，而不是说出的那句话。还是同一个“使确定”，只是从听者的心里移到了世上的一个事实。

senses.title: Too much sureness of oneself
senses.definition: impudence or presumption in manner (18th-century shading, now rare)
senses.definitionCN: 举止上的放肆、冒昧（18 世纪色彩，今罕用）
senses.example: He had the assurance to ask for a raise in his first week.
senses.exampleCN: 他竟有脸在上班第一周就要求加薪。
senses.why: The word had a negative tinge in the 18c., often suggesting impudence or presumption. There is a point where being sure of oneself stops looking like calm and starts looking like a claim on others.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 18 世纪带有贬义色彩，常指放肆或冒昧。对自己有把握，到某一点就不再像从容，而像对别人提要求。

senses.title: The deed that makes a right sure
senses.titleCN: 担保契据：让权利站得住的那张纸
senses.definition: a formal deed or clause that makes a right, title, or payment certain (legal)
senses.definitionCN: 使权利、所有权或付款成为确定的正式契据或条款（法律）
senses.example: The solicitor prepared an assurance of the title for the buyer.
senses.exampleCN: 律师为买方准备了一份产权担保契据。
senses.why: English -ance nouns often name the instrument as well as the act. In conveyancing an assurance is the deed that makes a title sure, just as a promise makes a mind sure.
senses.whyCN: 英语的 -ance 名词常同时命名动作和凭据。在不动产转让中，assurance 就是让产权站得住的那张契据，正如承诺让一颗心站得住。

intro.en: Assurance is assure plus -ance. Assure came through Old French asseurer from Vulgar Latin *assecurar, ad- 'to' plus securus 'free from care'; -ance makes an abstract noun of the act or state. The shift runs from 'making someone care-free' to 'a pledge', to 'certainty', to 'self-confidence', and finally to 'insurance'.
intro.cn: assurance 是 assure 加 -ance。assure 经古法语 asseurer 来自俗拉丁语 *assecurar，即 ad-“向”加 securus“无忧”；-ance 把动作或状态变成抽象名词。语义从“使某人无忧”走到“承诺”，再到“确定”“自信”，最后到“保险”。

items.en: Securus meant 'free from care, safe, secure', built from se- 'without, apart' plus cura 'care, anxiety'. The adjective describes a person, not a lock: to be secure is to have no care in the mind.
items.cn: securus 意为“无忧的、安全的、稳固的”，由 se-“无、离开”加 cura“忧虑、照料”构成。这个形容词描述的是人，不是锁：secure 就是心里没有忧虑。

items.en: The verb *assecurar, ad- plus securus, meant 'to make free from care'. The starred form is a reconstruction with no written record, so its exact shape is marked source uncertain; only its descendants in French and English are attested.
items.cn: 动词 *assecurar 由 ad- 加 securus 构成，意为“使无忧”。带星号的形式是没有书面记录的重构，因此其确切形态标为“来源不确定”；只有它在法语和英语中的后裔有文献可证。

items.en: Asseurer meant 'to reassure, calm, protect, to render sure', and the noun asseurance (11c.) meant 'assurance, promise; truce; certainty, safety, security'. Old French had already spread the word across trust, calm, and safety.
items.cn: asseurer 意为“使安心、使平静、保护、使确定”，名词 asseurance（11 世纪）意为“保证、承诺；停战；确定、安全、稳固”。古法语已经把这个词铺展到信任、平静与安全三个方面。

items.en: Assurance enters English as both 'formal or solemn pledge, promise' and 'certainty, full confidence'. Assure follows in the same period, meaning 'reassure, give confidence to; make secure; bind by a pledge'.
items.cn: assurance 进入英语时兼有“正式或郑重承诺”与“确定、充分信心”两义。assure 也在同一时期出现，意为“使安心、给信心；使安全；以承诺约束”。

items.en: 'Self-confident' is recorded from the 1590s. In the 18c. the word took a negative tinge, often suggesting impudence or presumption: too much assurance became a social fault.
items.cn: “自信”义记录于 16 世纪 90 年代。到 18 世纪，这个词带上贬义色彩，常指放肆或冒昧：过多的 assurance 成了一种社交过失。

items.en: Assurance was the older term for commercial insurance from the late 16c.; insurance, its en- variant, became standard in the 1650s. In the 20c. quality assurance turned the promise into a procedure, and the word acquired its modern office meaning.
items.cn: 从 16 世纪末起，assurance 是商业保险的较早说法；它的 en- 变体 insurance 在 17 世纪 50 年代成为标准。20 世纪，quality assurance 把承诺变成流程，这个词又添了现代的企业部门义。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on sure/secur-: insurance and reassure are true relatives with different prefixes. Endurance merely rhymes in shape and comes from durus 'hard', so it must be kept apart.
note.cn: 形近组建立在 sure/secur- 上：insurance 与 reassure 都是换前缀的真同族。endurance 只是外形相押，来自 durus“坚硬”，必须分开。

entries.tag: en- variant of the same word
entries.definition: cover against loss in exchange for payment. It is the en- twin of assurance and now the standard commercial term.
entries.definitionCN: 以付费换取损失保障。它是 assurance 的 en- 双胞胎，如今是标准的商业术语。

entries.definition: to make someone sure or free from doubt. Assurance is the state or act that the verb produces.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人确定、使免于疑虑。assurance 是这动词所产生的状态或行为。

entries.definition: comfort given to remove fear a second time. It repeats the making-sure with re-.
entries.definitionCN: 再次消除恐惧的安慰。它用 re- 重复了“使确定”这个动作。

entries.definition: the power to bear hardship, from durus 'hard'. The -ance ending is shared, the root is not.
entries.definitionCN: 忍耐力，来自 durus“坚硬”。词尾 -ance 相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: a promise that something will be done or will work. It is the most enforceable synonym of assurance.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事将做到或能奏效的承诺。它是 assurance 最具可执行性的同义词。

entries.definition: a serious promise, often with something given as security. It matches the formal tone of assurance.
entries.definitionCN: 郑重的承诺，常以某物作担保。它对应 assurance 的正式语气。

entries.definition: the quality of being definitely true or known. It is assurance as a state of mind or fact.
entries.definitionCN: 确定无疑的性质。它是作为心理或事实状态的 assurance。

entries.definition: belief in one's own or another's ability. It overlaps assurance in both the self and the promise senses.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己或他人能力的信任。它在“自信”和“可托付”两层上都与 assurance 重叠。

entries.definition: a written promise that goods will be repaired or replaced. It is assurance limited to a product.
entries.definitionCN: 对商品将维修或更换的书面承诺。它是被限定在商品上的 assurance。

normalIntro.en: The links are real: ad- 'to', securus 'free from care', -ance 'state of'. Assurance is literally the act of putting someone beyond care.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：ad-“向”、securus“无忧”、-ance“状态”。assurance 字面上就是把某人放到忧虑之外。

normal.en: assurance = as- (ad-, 'to') + sure ('certain') + -ance: making someone certain.
normal.cn: assurance = as-（ad-，“向”）+ sure（“确定”）+ -ance：使某人确定。

normal.en: The sure family runs through assure, reassure, ensure, insure, and secure.
normal.cn: sure 词族贯穿 assure、reassure、ensure、insure、secure。

normal.en: Insurance is the en- twin of assurance: same promise, different prefix.
normal.cn: insurance 是 assurance 的 en- 双胞胎：同一个承诺，不同的前缀。

normal.en: Quality assurance is a promise turned into a checklist.
normal.cn: quality assurance 是被做成了检查表的承诺。

normal.en: To speak with assurance is to sound as if your words had already been checked.
normal.cn: speak with assurance，就是听起来像你的话已经被核对过了。

abstract.en: Sureness is pictured as a weight lifted off the chest: securus is literally 'without care'.
abstract.cn: “确定”被画成从胸口搬走的一块重物：securus 字面就是“没有忧虑”。

abstract.en: The word travels from the hearer's mind to the speaker's manner: first you calm him, then you look calm yourself.
abstract.cn: 这个词从听者的心里走到说者的姿态：先让他安定，再让自己看起来安定。

abstract.en: A promise, a policy, and a deed are three ways of writing the same sentence: this will not fail you.
abstract.cn: 一句承诺、一份保单、一张契据，是同一句话的三种写法：它不会辜负你。

examples.en: The minister refused to give any assurance about the timing of the vote.
examples.cn: 部长拒绝就投票时间作出任何保证。

examples.en: She answered the hostile questions with the assurance of a practised speaker.
examples.cn: 她以老练演讲者的自信回答了那些敌意提问。

examples.en: In Britain, life assurance is often sold alongside a mortgage.
examples.cn: 在英国，人寿保险常与按揭一起销售。

dict_mnemonic.text: as（去）+ sure（确定）+ ance（名词）——去把“确定”给他，就是保证；谐音“额秀润斯”：额（我）秀（sure）润（ance）——拍胸脯让他放心 → assurance 保证；自信

root: 源自拉丁语 securus“无忧的”（se-“无”+ cura“忧虑”），经俗拉丁语 *assecurar、古法语 asseurer 进入英语；-ance 为抽象名词后缀，核心是“使某人心里无忧、确定”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one removal of care. A promise takes doubt out of another mind; certainty and self-confidence keep it out of one's own; insurance and quality assurance sell the removal; and too much of it turns into impudence.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一次“拿走忧虑”。承诺把疑虑从别人心里拿走；确定与自信把它从自己心里拿走；保险与质量保证把这次“拿走”拿来出售；而拿走得太多，就变成了厚颜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: making someone care-free — a hand on the shoulder, a word given, a policy signed.
core.cn: 核心意象：使某人无忧——一只手按在肩上，一句话给出，一份保单签下。

branches.en: THE PROMISE AND THE CALM: the word given, and the relief it leaves in the hearer.
branches.cn: 承诺与安心：给出的那句话，以及它在听者心里留下的宽慰。

branches.en: CERTAINTY AND SAFEGUARD: a fact held sure in the mind, and a fact made sure in the world.
branches.cn: 确定与保障：在心里被拿稳的事实，以及在世上被确保的事实。

branches.en: SELF-ASSURANCE: the calm of the capable, sliding into the impudence of the over-sure.
branches.cn: 自信：能者的从容，滑向过度自信者的放肆。

branches.en: THE INDUSTRIAL FORMS: a policy sold against loss, a procedure built to prevent it.
branches.cn: 制度化形态：为抵御损失而卖的保单，为预防损失而建的流程。

branches.en: THE DEED: the same making-sure written down and sealed.
branches.cn: 契据：同一个“使确定”被写下来并盖了章。

intro.en: Assurance is assure plus -ance. Assure is ad- plus the sure/secur- base, so the word is prefix, root, and abstract ending in that order. The ending lets the same noun mean the act of assuring and the state of being assured.
intro.cn: assurance 是 assure 加 -ance。assure 是 ad- 加 sure/secur- 词根，所以整词依次是前缀、词根、抽象后缀。后缀让同一个名词既能指“使确定”的动作，也能指“已确定”的状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin securus 'free from care' (se- 'without' + cura 'care') is the root of sure, secure, security, assure, assurance, insure and insurance. The prefixes ad-, re-, in-, en- each redirect the same 'care-free' idea.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 securus“无忧”（se-“无”+ cura“忧虑”）是 sure、secure、security、assure、assurance、insure、insurance 的词根。前缀 ad-、re-、in-、en- 各自把同一个“无忧”观念转向不同方向。

items.meaning: to make someone free from doubt
items.example: He assured her that the door had been locked.
items.exampleCN: 他向她保证门已经锁好了。

items.example: She needed an assurance before she signed.
items.exampleCN: 签字之前她需要一个保证。

items.example: Are you sure the key is in your bag?
items.exampleCN: 你确定钥匙在你包里吗？

items.example: The documents are secure in the vault.
items.exampleCN: 文件在保险库里很安全。

items.meaning: to make certain against loss by paying
items.example: They insured the painting for two million.
items.exampleCN: 他们为这幅画投保了两百万。
这份保单包含旅行保险。

items.meaning: to make something certain to happen
items.example: Please ensure that the window is closed.
An assured income let him write full time.
items.exampleCN: 一份有保障的收入让他能全职写作。

definition_zh: 银河系的；星系的；银河系尺度的；极大的（口语夸张）
definition_en: of or relating to a galaxy, especially the Milky Way, or to the whole star system that contains the sun
core_image: 一枚从侧面看去的旋涡盘，中心鼓起，几条旋臂向外拖开，盘面薄得像一张纸
scene: 夜里没有月光的山顶，一条灰白色光带横过天顶，望远镜正对着它的中心方向。 Above the ridge, a faint band of light marks the galactic plane.
sceneCN: 这里 galactic 指「与银河系盘面有关的」（第 3 个义项：用于银河系中心、盘面、银晕等结构术语）；句意为山脊之上一条淡淡光带标出了银河系盘面。图中可辨识物件：无月的夜空、乳白光带、指向天顶的望远镜、山脊轮廓、星点。

pos.zh: 银河系的；星系的；（口语）极大的、银河级的

collocations.zh: 银河年（太阳绕银心一周）

senses.title: Belonging to the Milky Way
senses.definition: relating to the Milky Way, the galaxy that contains the sun and its planets
senses.definitionCN: 与包含太阳及其行星的银河系有关的
senses.example: Dust clouds hide the galactic centre from optical telescopes.
senses.exampleCN: 尘埃云使光学望远镜看不见银河系中心。
senses.why: the adjective was formed in English from galaxy plus -ic, and its first and still central use is to name the one galaxy we live inside.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由 galaxy 加 -ic 在英语中构成，最早也最核心的用法就是称呼我们身处的这个星系。

senses.title: Belonging to galaxies in general
senses.definition: relating to galaxies as a class of objects rather than to the Milky Way alone
senses.definitionCN: 指作为一类天体的星系，而非仅指银河系
senses.example: Galactic surveys map how star formation changes from galaxy to galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: 星系巡天描绘出恒星形成如何从一个星系到另一个星系发生变化。
senses.why: once astronomers knew that many such star systems exist, the same adjective was extended from one proper name to the whole class.
senses.whyCN: 当天文学家确认这类恒星系统有许多个之后，同一个形容词便从一个专名扩展到了整个类别。

senses.title: Structural terms of a galaxy
senses.titleCN: 银河系结构的术语用法
senses.definition: used in fixed compounds that name the parts of a galaxy, such as plane, centre, disk, bulge and halo
senses.definitionCN: 用于「盘面、中心、盘、核球、银晕」等固定搭配，指星系的各个结构部分
senses.example: Above the ridge, a faint band of light marks the galactic plane.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊之上，一条淡淡的光带标出了银河系盘面。
senses.why: a galaxy is a flattened system, so astronomers name its geometry the way geographers name a globe: plane, centre, disk, halo.
senses.whyCN: 星系是一个扁平的体系，因此天文学家像地理学家描述地球那样给它命名：盘面、中心、盘、晕。

senses.title: The galactic year
senses.titleCN: 银河年：太阳绕银心一周的时长
senses.definition: used in the phrase galactic year for the time the sun takes to travel once around the Milky Way's centre
senses.definitionCN: 用于 galactic year，指太阳绕银河系中心运行一周所需的时间
senses.example: One galactic year is roughly two hundred and thirty million earthly years.
senses.exampleCN: 一个银河年大约是两亿三千万个地球年。
senses.why: the adjective turns a duration into a galactic one: the same idea of a year, measured around a different centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把一段时长换算到星系尺度：同样是「一年」的概念，只是绕另一个中心来计量。

senses.title: Halo, bulge and dark matter
senses.titleCN: 银晕、核球与暗物质语境
senses.definition: used of the faint outer and inner parts of a galaxy that are studied through stars, gas and gravity
senses.definitionCN: 指星系外围与内部那些通过恒星、气体和引力来研究的暗淡部分
senses.example: The galactic halo holds old stars and most of the galaxy's dark matter.
senses.exampleCN: 银晕容纳着老年恒星以及该星系的大部分暗物质。
senses.why: these parts emit little light, so they are named by position and studied indirectly, which is why the adjective appears so often beside them.
senses.whyCN: 这些部分发出光很少，只能按位置命名并间接研究，因此这个形容词常与它们同现。

senses.title: Enormous, on a cosmic scale
senses.titleCN: 夸张用法：极大的、银河级的
senses.definition: used informally for something enormous or far-reaching, as if measured on the scale of a galaxy
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容某事物极其巨大或影响深远，仿佛以星系为尺度衡量
senses.example: The paperwork failure was a galactic mistake rather than a small one.
senses.exampleCN: 那次文书失误不是小错，而是一场银河级的大错。
senses.why: the adjective imports the largest unit speakers know, so it works as a hyperbole for size rather than as an astronomy term.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词借用了说话者所知最大的单位，于是成为夸张尺寸的说法，而非天文学术语。

senses.title: Science-fiction settings
senses.definition: used in fiction for empires, fleets or federations that span a whole galaxy
senses.definitionCN: 在虚构作品中指横跨整个星系的帝国、舰队或联邦
senses.example: The novel opens with a galactic empire losing contact with its outer worlds.
senses.exampleCN: 小说开篇写一个银河帝国与它的外围世界失去联系。
senses.why: fiction needs a word for the largest political unit imaginable, and the astronomical adjective supplies it without inventing anything.
senses.whyCN: 虚构作品需要一个词来形容想象中最大的政治单位，而天文学形容词正好提供了它，无须另造新词。

senses.title: Old sense: of milk
senses.definition: formerly meaning 'of milk', a sense kept only in the word's history and in related scientific terms
senses.definitionCN: 旧时意为「乳汁的」，此义仅存于词史与相关科学术语中
senses.example: The older medical sense of galactic survives only in etymological notes.
senses.exampleCN: galactic 古老的医学义「乳汁的」只保留在词源注释里。
senses.why: the Greek source galaxias meant 'milky', so the adjective once belonged to milk before astronomy took it over.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源头 galaxias 意为「乳色的」，因此这个形容词在被天文学接管之前曾属于「奶」。

intro.en: Galactic comes from Greek galaxias (kyklos) 'the milky circle', from gala, galaktos 'milk', with the English suffix -ic. The astronomical sense was fixed in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: galactic 来自希腊语 galaxias（kyklos）「乳色的圆环」，源于 gala、galaktos「奶」，加英语后缀 -ic。天文学义在 19 世纪固定下来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek galaxias meant 'milky', used of the pale band across the night sky; the full phrase was galaxias kyklos, 'the milky circle'.
items.cn: 希腊语 galaxias 意为「乳色的」，用于指夜空中那条淡白光带；完整说法是 galaxias kyklos「乳色的圆环」。

items.en: The root is gala, galaktos 'milk'. The same element appears in galactose, a sugar once obtained from milk.
items.cn: 词根是 gala、galaktos「奶」。同一成分出现在 galactose 中，那是一种最初从奶中取得的糖。

items.en: Latin calqued the Greek phrase as via lactea 'the milky way', literally 'the milky road', which is the source of the English name Milky Way.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊短语仿译为 via lactea「乳色的路」，字面是「奶做的路」，这就是英语名称 Milky Way 的来源。

items.en: English formed galactic from the Greek stem in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, as telescopes resolved the band into stars and then into a disk of stars.
items.cn: 英语在 18 至 19 世纪用希腊词干构成 galactic，正值望远镜把那条光带解析为恒星、再解析为一个恒星盘。

items.en: Twentieth-century astronomy extended the adjective to every galaxy, and popular speech borrowed it for anything enormous.
items.cn: 20 世纪的天文学把这个形容词扩展到所有星系，日常口语又借它来形容任何巨大的事物。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek origin of gala is not settled, and the Indo-European form often cited for 'milk' is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：gala 在希腊语之前的来源尚无定论，常被引用的那个表示「奶」的印欧形式属于重构形式，而非有记录的词。

note.en: Group one holds words sharing the same galactic stem; group two holds adjectives of the sky that are close in use but not in root.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 galactic 词干的词；第二组是用法相近但词根不同的天空类形容词。

entries.definition: The noun from which galactic is formed: a gravitationally bound system of stars, gas and dust.
entries.definitionCN: 构成 galactic 的名词：由引力束缚的恒星、气体与尘埃系统。

entries.definition: Inter- 'between' plus galactic: belonging to the space between galaxies, not inside one.
entries.definitionCN: inter-「之间」加 galactic：属于星系之间的空间，而非星系内部。

entries.definition: Extra- 'outside' plus galactic: lying beyond our own galaxy, as extragalactic nebulae do.
entries.definitionCN: extra-「在外」加 galactic：位于我们星系之外，如河外星云。

entries.definition: From Greek gala 'milk' plus -ose, the sugar suffix; it shares the milk root but has no astronomical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊 gala「奶」加糖类后缀 -ose 构成；共享「奶」的词根，但没有天文学含义。

entries.definition: Relating to the universe as a whole, from Greek kosmos 'order'; wider than galactic, which stops at one galaxy.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个宇宙有关，来自希腊 kosmos「秩序」；比只到星系一级的 galactic 更广。

entries.definition: Relating to astronomy, or informally to numbers too large to grasp; it names the discipline, not the galaxy.
entries.definitionCN: 与天文学有关，口语中也指数值大得难以想象；它指学科，而非星系。

entries.definition: Relating to stars, from Latin stella; a galactic system is made of stars, but the words mark different levels.
entries.definitionCN: 与恒星有关，来自拉丁 stella；星系由恒星组成，但两词标示的层级不同。

entries.definition: Belonging to the sky or heavens, from Latin caelum; it covers everything overhead, galactic or not.
entries.definitionCN: 属于天空或天界，来自拉丁 caelum；涵盖头顶一切，无论是否属于星系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek gala 'milk' + -ic: the Milky Way was named for looking like a stream of milk.
normal.cn: 希腊 gala「奶」+ -ic：银河得名于它看上去像一道奶流。

normal.en: Latin said via lactea 'milky road', which English copied as the Milky Way.
normal.cn: 拉丁语说 via lactea「奶做的路」，英语照抄为 the Milky Way。

normal.en: The family runs galaxy, galaxies, galactic, intergalactic, extragalactic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 galaxy、galaxies、galactic、intergalactic、extragalactic。

normal.en: Fixed compounds place it in astronomy: galactic centre, galactic plane, galactic halo.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它固定在天文学中：银河系中心、银河系盘面、银晕。

normal.en: One galactic year is the sun's own orbit around the galaxy's centre.
normal.cn: 一个银河年就是太阳绕星系中心自己的一圈。

abstract.en: Picture a fried egg seen edge-on: a bright yolk and a thin white disk.
abstract.cn: 想象一只侧看过去的煎蛋：亮的蛋黄与薄薄的蛋白盘。

abstract.en: Picture a clock so large that its single tick lasts a human lifetime.
abstract.cn: 想象一只大得离谱的钟，一次滴答就耗尽人的一生。

abstract.en: Picture a city map where the streets are spiral arms and the centre is a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一张城市地图，街道是旋臂，中心是一片人潮。

examples.en: Radio telescopes can see through the dust that hides the galactic centre.
examples.cn: 射电望远镜能穿透遮住银河系中心的尘埃。

examples.en: The team measured the galaxy's mass from the motion of its galactic halo.
examples.cn: 团队根据银晕的运动测出了该星系的质量。

examples.en: A galactic year is far longer than any human record.
examples.cn: 一个银河年远比任何人类记录都要长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尬了（gala）＋克体（-ctic）」——银河大得让人尴尬地磕巴 → 银河系的

root: 希腊 galaxias（kyklos）「乳色的圆环」= gala、galaktos「奶」+ 形容词后缀 -ic；拉丁仿译为 via lactea，英语据此称 the Milky Way。gala 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one widening ring: the Milky Way's own adjective, then galaxies as a class, then their named parts, then a year measured around a centre, then the unseen halo, then sheer size, fiction and finally the word's milky past.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一圈逐步扩大：先是我们所在银河系的形容词，再是作为类别的星系，再是其各部分的名称，然后是绕中心计量的一年，接着是看不见的银晕，再到纯粹的巨大、虚构设定，最后回到这个词与「奶」的旧缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin bright disk seen edge-on, with a swollen centre and arms dragging outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个侧看过去的薄亮盘面，中心鼓起，旋臂向外拖开。

branches.en: ONE AND MANY: the same adjective names our galaxy and then any galaxy.
branches.cn: 一个与许多：同一个形容词先指我们的星系，再指任何星系。

branches.en: MAP OF A DISK: plane, centre and halo are directions on the same flattened system.
branches.cn: 盘面地图：盘面、中心与银晕是同一个扁平体系上的方位。

branches.en: CLOCK AROUND A CENTRE: a year redefined by what it goes around.
branches.cn: 绕中心的钟：把「一年」按所绕的中心重新定义。

branches.en: BORROWED MAGNITUDE: speech and fiction take the largest unit as a figure of speech.
branches.cn: 借来的量级：口语与虚构作品把最大的单位借作修辞。

branches.en: MILKY ORIGIN: the name was about milk before it was about stars.
branches.cn: 乳色源头：这个名字先与奶有关，后来才与恒星有关。

intro.en: Galactic is a Greek stem plus an English adjective suffix; the stem also builds the noun galaxy and several compounds.
intro.cn: galactic 是希腊词干加英语形容词后缀；同一词干还构成名词 galaxy 及若干复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin kept the same milk image in lac 'milk', lacteus 'milky' and via lactea 'the milky road', the direct model of the English name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 lac「奶」、lacteus「乳色的」与 via lactea「奶做的路」保留了同一幅奶的意象，后者正是英语名称的直接模板。

items.example: The root names the pale band the Greeks thought looked like milk.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名了希腊人觉得像奶的那条淡白光带。

items.meaning: belonging to; of the nature of
items.example: The suffix turns the noun galaxy into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词 galaxy 变成形容词。

items.example: A faint band marks the galactic plane.
items.exampleCN: 一条淡光带标出银河系盘面。

items.example: The galaxy contains billions of stars.
items.exampleCN: 这个星系包含数十亿颗恒星。

items.example: Distant galaxies look like faint smudges.
items.exampleCN: 遥远的星系看上去像淡淡的小污点。

items.example: Extragalactic astronomy began with nebula debates.
items.exampleCN: 河外天文学始于关于星云的争论。

items.example: The two clouds are galactically close.
items.exampleCN: 这两团云在星系尺度上算得很近。

items.meaning: a sugar once derived from milk
items.meaningCN: 一种最初从奶中取得的糖
items.exampleCN: 半乳糖是乳糖的组成部分。

latinEntries.structure: lacteus, lactea, lacteum (adj., first and second declension)
via lactea (noun phrase, first declension + adjective)
latinEntries.meaning: the Milky Way, literally 'the milky road'

definition_zh: 遗传；遗传性；（旧义）继承
definition_en: the transmission of traits from parents to offspring, or the set of inherited characteristics of an organism
core_image: 同一对父母养大的子女，身高与性格却各有差别，差别像从看不见的账本里带出来的
scene: 同一对父母养大的子女，身高与性格却各有差别。 Researchers separate the effects of heredity from those of upbringing.
sceneCN: 这里 heredity 指「亲代把性状传给子代的生物过程」（第 1 个义项：性状的遗传传递）；句意为研究者把遗传的影响与养育的影响分开。可辨识物件：并排的身高尺、两张性格记录表、家谱图、双栏表格。

pos.zh: 遗传；遗传性
（旧义）继承；继承权

senses.title: Transmission of traits
senses.definition: the passing of characteristics from parents to offspring
senses.definitionCN: 特征由亲代传给子代
senses.example: Heredity explains why siblings resemble their parents.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传解释了为什么兄弟姐妹像他们的父母。
senses.why: The word names the process itself, not the genes that carry it, which is why it pairs naturally with environment.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名过程本身，而非承载它的基因，因此天然与「环境」配对。

senses.title: An organism's inherited constitution
senses.definition: the total set of inherited characteristics of an organism
senses.definitionCN: 一个生物体所继承的全部特征
senses.example: Heredity and environment interact in development.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传与环境在发育中相互作用。
senses.why: The process sense and the constitution sense share a form: what is transmitted becomes what an organism carries.
senses.whyCN: 过程义与组成义共用一词形：被传下的东西成为生物体所携带的东西。

senses.title: The study of inheritance
senses.definition: the field or subject concerned with transmission of traits
senses.definitionCN: 研究性状传递的领域或学科
senses.example: Heredity was studied long before genes were named.
senses.exampleCN: 早在基因被命名之前，人们就在研究遗传。
senses.why: The name of the process also names the subject that studies it, so heredity can stand for a field of inquiry.
senses.whyCN: 过程之名也命名研究它的学科，因此 heredity 可以指一个研究领域。

senses.title: Laws of heredity
senses.definition: the regular patterns by which traits appear in later generations
senses.definitionCN: 性状在后代中出现的规律模式
senses.example: Mendel's laws of heredity describe the ratios of traits.
senses.exampleCN: 孟德尔的遗传规律描述了性状的比例。
senses.why: Once patterns were counted, heredity could be spoken of as having laws rather than merely effects.
senses.whyCN: 一旦模式可以被计数，遗传就可以被说成有规律，而不只是有效应。

senses.title: Heredity versus environment
senses.definition: the relative contribution of inherited and environmental factors
senses.definitionCN: 遗传因素与环境因素的相对贡献
senses.example: The debate over heredity and environment has softened.
senses.exampleCN: 关于遗传与环境的争论已经缓和。
senses.why: The word became a pole in a debate, so heredity often appears opposite environment rather than alone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词成了争论中的一极，因此 heredity 常与 environment 相对出现，而非单独使用。

senses.title: Heredity as a biological force
senses.definition: the influence of inherited factors on development and behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 遗传因素对发育与行为的影响
senses.example: Heredity sets limits that nutrition can only partly shift.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传设定了界限，营养只能部分改变。
senses.why: When treated as a force, heredity explains the range of possible development rather than a single fixed result.
senses.whyCN: 当被当作一种力量时，遗传解释的是发育的可能范围，而非单一固定结果。

senses.title: Heredity in breeding
senses.definition: the transmission that breeders rely on when fixing traits
senses.definitionCN: 育种者固定性状时所依赖的传递
senses.example: Heredity determines which traits a breeder can fix.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传决定育种者能固定哪些性状。
senses.why: Breeders work with heredity as a practical constraint: some traits can be fixed, others cannot.
senses.whyCN: 育种者把遗传当作实际限制来工作：有些性状可以固定，有些不能。

senses.title: Archaic legal inheritance
senses.definition: the old sense of inheriting property or a right
senses.definitionCN: 继承财产或权利的旧义
senses.example: In older legal writing, heredity meant the right to inherit.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的法律文本中，heredity 指继承权。
senses.why: The legal sense is the oldest layer of the word, preserved in older statutes rather than in modern biology.
senses.whyCN: 法律义是这个词最古老的层次，保存在较早的法条中，而非现代生物学中。

intro.en: Heredity was borrowed from Latin hereditas 'inheritance, heirship', from heres (hered-) 'heir'.
intro.cn: heredity 直接借自拉丁 hereditas「继承、继承权」，其词干为 heres（hered-）「继承人」。

items.en: Heres (genitive heredis) meant 'heir'. Its deeper origin is not established; related forms in other Indo-European languages are hypotheses, and any PIE form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: heres（属格 heredis）意为「继承人」。其更深来源未得到确证；其他印欧语中的相关形式只是假说，任何原始印欧语形式均属重构。

items.en: Hereditas meant 'inheritance, heirship'; English heredity was borrowed directly from this Latin noun rather than through French.
items.cn: hereditas 意为「继承、继承权」；英语 heredity 直接借自这个拉丁名词，而非经法语。

items.en: The word appears in English by the sixteenth century with the legal sense 'inheritance'; the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在 16 世纪已以「继承」的法律义出现在英语中；确切的最早书证不确定。

items.en: In the nineteenth century heredity was reshaped into the biological term for the transmission of traits, as breeding and cell theory advanced.
items.cn: 19 世纪，随着育种与细胞理论进展，heredity 被重塑为性状传递的生物学术语。

items.en: Twentieth-century genetics narrowed heredity to the transmission itself, distinct from the genes that carry it.
items.cn: 20 世纪的遗传学把 heredity 收窄为传递过程本身，与承载它的基因区分开。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-Latin origin of heres is unsettled, and the shift from legal to biological use is not sharply dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：heres 的拉丁语之前来源未有定论，从法律义到生物学义的转变也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one separates heredity from same-root words with different grammar; group two separates it from the words for inheritance, lineage and the science of genes.
note.cn: 第一组把 heredity 与同根但语法角色不同的词分开；第二组把它与继承、世系、基因科学相关词区分。

entries.definition: The adjective describing what is transmitted; heredity is the process or constitution itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述被传递之物的形容词；heredity 是过程或组成本身。

entries.definition: What is handed down, especially culture or family property; it is not the biological process.
entries.definitionCN: 指被传下的东西，尤其是文化或家族财产；不是生物过程。

entries.definition: Able to be inherited; the word describes a possibility, while heredity names the actual transmission.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被继承；描述可能性，而 heredity 命名实际传递。

entries.definition: A person or doctrine stressing heredity as a cause of differences; it belongs to debate rather than biology alone.
entries.definitionCN: 强调遗传是差异原因的人或学说；属于争论语境，而非单纯生物学。

entries.definition: A broader word covering legal property and biological transmission; heredity is the biological process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 较宽泛的词，涵盖法定财产与生物传递；heredity 是生物过程本身。

entries.definition: The modern science of genes; heredity names the transmission that genetics explains.
entries.definitionCN: 研究基因的现代科学；heredity 命名遗传学所要解释的传递。

entries.definition: Ancestry or lineage, especially as a line of descent; heredity is the mechanism, descent is the line.
entries.definitionCN: 指血统或世系，尤指一条下传的线；heredity 是机制，descent 是那条线。

entries.tag: the general act of passing on
entries.definition: A neutral term for passing anything from one generation to the next, biological or not.
entries.definitionCN: 中性词，指把任何东西传给下一代，不论是否生物性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: heres 'heir' + -ity: the state of being inherited.
normal.cn: heres「继承人」+ -ity：被继承的状态。

normal.en: The family runs heredity, hereditary, hereditarily and hereditarian.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 heredity、hereditary、hereditarily 与 hereditarian。

normal.en: The fixed pair is heredity and environment.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是遗传与环境。

normal.en: Laws of heredity were counted before genes were named.
normal.cn: 在基因被命名之前，遗传规律就已被计数。

normal.en: Modern genetics separates heredity from the genes that carry it.
normal.cn: 现代遗传学把遗传过程与承载它的基因分开。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible ledger that each child receives with a few entries already filled in.
abstract.cn: 想象每个孩子都收到一本看不见的账本，上面已写好几笔。

abstract.en: Picture two seeds from one pod landing in different soils.
abstract.cn: 想象同一豆荚里的两粒种子落在不同的土里。

abstract.en: Picture a hand of cards dealt before anyone chooses how to play.
abstract.cn: 想象一手牌在任何人决定怎么打之前就已发好。

examples.en: Heredity alone does not explain the difference between the twins.
examples.cn: 单靠遗传解释不了这对双胞胎的差异。

examples.en: Breeders rely on heredity when they select for a fixed coat colour.
examples.cn: 育种者选育固定毛色时依赖遗传。

examples.en: The old statute used heredity in the sense of a right to inherit.
examples.cn: 旧法规用 heredity 指继承权。

dict_mnemonic.text: hered（继承人）+ ity（名词尾）——继承人接到的东西 → 遗传；旧义才是「继承」。

root: 拉丁 hereditas「继承、继承权」← heres（hered-）「继承人」；heres 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a current running through generations: the process, the constitution it produces, the study of it, its laws, its debate with environment, its force, its use in breeding and its old legal sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一股穿越世代的电流展开：传递过程、由此形成的组成、对它的研究、它的规律、它与环境的争论、它的力量、它在育种中的用途，以及旧时的法律义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible ledger handed to each child with a few entries already filled in.
core.cn: 核心意象：每个孩子都收到一本看不见的账本，上面已写好几笔。

branches.en: PROCESS AND FORCE: transmission itself, and the influence it exerts on development.
branches.cn: 过程与力量：传递本身，以及它对发育施加的影响。

branches.en: CONSTITUTION AND BREEDING: what an organism carries, and what a breeder can fix.
branches.cn: 组成与育种：生物体携带什么，育种者能固定什么。

branches.en: STUDY: the field that examines transmission before and after genes were named.
branches.cn: 研究：在基因被命名前后考察传递的领域。

branches.en: LAWS AND DEBATE: counted ratios, and the argument with environment.
branches.cn: 规律与争论：可计数的比例，以及与环境的论战。

branches.en: OLD LAW: the archaic sense of a right to inherit property.
branches.cn: 旧法律：继承财产之权利的古老义。

intro.en: Heredity is a Latin noun built on the hered- stem; the same stem forms the legal and biological words around it.
intro.cn: heredity 是建立在 hered- 词干上的拉丁名词；同一词干构成周围的法律与生物词。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres (hered-) gives hereditas, hereditarius, heredity, hereditary and inherit; no prefix is involved in heredity itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 heres（hered-）衍生 hereditas、hereditarius、heredity、hereditary 与 inherit；heredity 本身不含前缀。

items.example: The stem names the person who receives.
Hereditas is the direct source of heredity.
items.exampleCN: hereditas 是 heredity 的直接来源。
这个形容词提供了 hereditary。

items.example: The suffix turns the stem into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词干变成状态名词。
这一性状以遗传方式传递。
继承人在契据上签了字。

latinEntries.meaning: to inherit, leave as an inheritance

definition_zh: 充实；使丰富；提高价值或品质
definition_en: to improve the quality or value of something, or to add interesting material to it
core_image: 往一杯清水里加入果汁与果肉，平淡的液体立刻有了滋味与颜色
scene: 她把同学们的反馈逐条吸收进方案，让报告更充实。 New feedback enriched the final report.
sceneCN: 这里 enrich 是「充实；使丰富」（第 1 个义项：提高品质或价值）；句意：新的反馈使最终报告更加充实。

pos.zh: 充实；使丰富；提高价值

senses.title: To raise the quality or value of something
senses.definition: to add something that makes a thing better, more interesting, or more useful
senses.definitionCN: 加入某些内容，使事物更好、更有趣或更有用
senses.example: Field trips enrich science lessons.
senses.exampleCN: 实地考察让科学课更加丰富。
senses.why: The prefix en- means to make, so the verb turns richness into something you give to another thing.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 表示「使成为」，因此这个动词把「丰富」变成你赋予他物的东西。

senses.title: To make land or food more nutritious
senses.definition: to add nutrients or valuable substances to soil, water, or food
senses.definitionCN: 向土壤、水源或食物中添加养分或有用物质
senses.example: Farmers enrich the field with compost.
senses.exampleCN: 农民用堆肥给田地增肥。
senses.why: The same idea of adding worth applies literally to soil, where what is added is nutrient rather than interest.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「添加价值」义项可本义用于土壤，只是所添加的是养分而非趣味。

senses.title: To increase the wealth of a person or group
senses.definition: to give someone or a group a great deal of money or resources
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某群体拥有大量金钱或资源
senses.example: The oil boom enriched a whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 石油热潮使整个地区变得富裕。
senses.why: Extended from material value to money, the verb can name the process that makes people financially rich.
senses.whyCN: 从物质价值延伸到金钱，这个动词可指使人变富的过程。

intro.en: Enrich pairs the prefix en- with rich, an adjective that English already had before the verb was built.
intro.cn: enrich 由前缀 en- 与 rich 组成；英语先有这个形容词，之后才造出动词。

items.en: Rice meant powerful or good, the ancestor of rich.
items.cn: rīce 意为强大的、优良的，是 rich 的前身。

items.en: The prefix en- was used to build verbs meaning to make something so.
items.cn: 前缀 en- 用来构成「使成为某种状态」的动词。

items.en: enricher appears in administrative records of England.
items.cn: enricher 出现在英国的行政文书中。

items.en: The verb spreads in the sense of making people wealthy.
items.cn: 该动词在「使人致富」义项上普及开来。

items.en: Abstract uses such as enriching experience become standard.
items.cn: 充实经验这类抽象用法成为现代表达。

note.en: Group one holds family words built on the same verb; group two holds other verbs of adding value.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词派生的同族词；第二组是其他表示增添价值的动词。

entries.definition: The action or result noun of the verb, common in mining and in education programmes.
entries.definitionCN: 该动词的动作或结果名词，常见于矿业与教育项目。

entries.definition: A person or machine that adds value; in water treatment it names the dosing unit.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或设备；在水处理中指添加装置。

entries.definition: The adjective that supplies the meaning; the prefix only turns it into an action.
entries.definitionCN: 提供核心义的形容词；前缀只把它变成动作。

entries.definition: Built the same way from dear, but the result is affection rather than abundance.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由 dear 加前缀构成，但结果是喜爱而非充裕。

entries.definition: To improve the appearance or value of something already good; less about adding new material.
entries.definitionCN: 提升本已不错之物的外观或价值，较少强调增添新内容。

entries.definition: To make stronger, often with added nutrients in food or drink.
entries.definitionCN: 使更强，常指在食物饮料中加入营养成分。

entries.definition: To supply what a living thing needs to grow; the biological side of adding value.
entries.definitionCN: 供给生长所需，是增添价值的生物层面。

entries.definition: To add decoration, sometimes to a story, so the gain may be ornamental rather than real.
entries.definitionCN: 添加装饰，有时用于故事，因此增益可能只是装饰性的。

normalIntro.en: Enrich contains rich, so the whole verb can be read as making something rich.
normalIntro.cn: enrich 内含 rich，因此整个动词可读作「使变得富有」。

normal.en: En- means to make, so enrich means to make rich.
normal.cn: en- 表示使，所以 enrich 就是使富有。

normal.en: Pair it with soil, curriculum, and life, the three things exams mention most.
normal.cn: 把它与土壤、课程、生活搭配，这是考试最常提的三个对象。

normal.en: Use enriched for the result and enriching for the activity itself.
normal.cn: enriched 表结果，enriching 表活动本身。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with enrich oneself, which stresses money rather than quality.
normal.cn: 不要与「致富」混淆，后者强调金钱而非品质。

normal.en: In writing, enrich replaces add value to with one verb.
normal.cn: 写作中，enrich 可一词替代 add value to。

abstract.en: Picture a plain bowl into which someone keeps pouring colorful fruit.
abstract.cn: 想象一只素碗，不断有人往里倒入彩色果肉。

abstract.en: Imagine a farmer turning dark compost into tired soil.
abstract.cn: 想象农夫把堆肥翻进疲惫的土地。

abstract.en: Think of a vault filling coin by coin until the door barely closes.
abstract.cn: 想象金库一枚枚堆币，直到库门将合不拢。

examples.en: Reading widely enriches your writing.
examples.cn: 广泛阅读会让你的写作更有内涵。

examples.en: The programme was enriched with local case studies.
examples.cn: 该项目加入了本地案例研究。

examples.en: Nothing enriches a city like a good library.
examples.cn: 没有什么比一座好图书馆更能充实一座城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因 rich」——因为想要 rich，所以去 enrich；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 rīce（强盛的）→ rich＋古法语前缀 en-（使成为）→ 盎格鲁-诺曼语 enricher → 中古英语 enrichen → 现代英语 enrich，核心义「使变得丰足」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with adding worth to a thing, moves to feeding soil and food, and ends with making people wealthy.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从为事物增添价值出发，转到为土壤与食物添加养分，最后落到使人富裕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something poured into a plain container until it overflows with value.
core.cn: 核心意象：不断往素器里注入东西，直到价值满溢。

branches.en: Adding worth to lessons and texts is the abstract core.
branches.cn: 为课程与文本增添价值，是抽象的核心用法。

branches.en: Feeding soil keeps the idea physical and agricultural.
branches.cn: 给土地施肥，让这个概念保持在农业实物层面。

branches.en: Money extends abundance to people and regions.
branches.cn: 金钱把充裕延伸到人与地区。

branches.en: Both senses describe adding something that was missing.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在说补入原本缺少之物。

branches.en: Fertile land and mineral wealth both turn into riches.
branches.cn: 肥沃土地与矿藏财富都会转化为财富。

intro.en: Enrich is a native verb with a French prefix, and its small family grows with English endings.
intro.cn: enrich 是带法语前缀的本族动词，其词族靠英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin divitis means wealthy and was used by scholars who translated the verb into legal Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 divitis 表示富裕，曾被把该动词转译为法律拉丁语的学者使用。

items.example: En- turns rich into a verb.
items.exampleCN: en- 把 rich 变成动词。

items.example: The old form is the source of modern rich.
items.exampleCN: 古形是现代 rich 的来源。

items.example: Uranium enrichment is a technical phrase.
items.exampleCN: 铀浓缩是一个技术短语。

items.meaning: a person or device that adds value
items.example: A soil enricher is sold in garden shops.
items.exampleCN: 土壤改良剂在花店有售。

items.example: It is the opposite of enrich.
items.exampleCN: 它是 enrich 的反义词。

definition_zh: 牵涉；需要；使成为必要结果；限定继承
definition_en: to involve something as a necessary part or result, or to require effort, cost, or time
core_image: 一份清单上，主任务后面用线串着几项不可避免的子任务
scene: 调往新岗位意味着要长期驻外，还要重新学习一套系统。 The assignment entails long stays abroad.
sceneCN: 这里 entail 是「牵涉；需要」（第 1 个义项：作为必要部分伴随而来）；句意：这项任务牵涉长期驻外。

pos.zh: 牵涉；需要；使成为必然结果
限定继承；被限定的遗产

derivatives.zh: 限定遗产的授予者（法律用语）

senses.title: To involve something as a necessary part
senses.titleCN: 牵涉；包含作为必要部分
senses.definition: to have something as an unavoidable part of a plan, role, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物作为计划、职位或情境中不可避免的一部分
senses.example: The job entails a great deal of travelling.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作需要大量出差。
senses.why: The old legal verb cut an estate so that duties came attached to it, so part of the sense is always something tied on.
senses.whyCN: 该词的法律古义是把产业连同义务一起划定，因此词义始终带有附带绑定的意味。

senses.title: To require effort, cost, or time
senses.definition: to make something necessary because of what follows from it
senses.definitionCN: 因其后果而使某事物成为必需
senses.example: Repairs will entail replacing the whole floor.
senses.exampleCN: 维修意味着更换整块地板。
senses.why: When the attached part is a price or labour, the verb shifts from containing to demanding.
senses.whyCN: 当附带的部分是代价或劳动时，动词从包含转向要求。

senses.title: To limit inheritance to fixed heirs
senses.definition: to settle property so that it can pass only to specified descendants
senses.definitionCN: 安排财产仅由指定后裔继承
senses.example: The estate was entailed to the eldest son.
senses.exampleCN: 这份遗产被限定由长子继承。
senses.why: This is the original legal use: the notch cut on a tally stick fixed who could inherit next.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的法律用法：在计数木条上刻出的缺口规定了下一位继承人。

intro.en: Entail began as a law term about cutting a tail of heirs onto an estate, from French tailler.
intro.cn: entail 原是法律术语，指为产业切出继承人的尾部，来自法语 tailler。

items.en: Taxiare gave the idea of cutting or arranging by notches.
items.cn: taxiare 给出刻痕整理之义。

items.en: Tailler means to cut, and taille is a notch or tally.
items.cn: tailler 意为切割，taille 指刻痕或计数条。

items.en: Entailler describes fixing the tail of heirs of a property.
items.cn: entailler 指固定财产的继承人序列。

items.en: The verb enters English charters and land records.
items.cn: 中古英语中该动词进入特许状与土地文书。

items.en: Figurative uses attach unavoidable conditions to plans.
items.cn: 近古英语时期出现把必然条件附于计划的比喻用法。

items.en: The general sense of involving as a necessity now dominates.
items.cn: 现代英语以「作为必要而牵涉」的通义为主。

note.en: Group one holds the noun and the rhyming borrowings; group two holds other verbs of necessity.
note.cn: 第一组是名词与同尾借词；第二组是其他表示必要的动词。

entries.definition: The noun, used for a legal settlement and for a relation between propositions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指限定继承与命题间的蕴含关系。

entries.definition: Same ending sound, different history: selling goods in small quantities.
entries.definitionCN: 尾部同音而来源不同，指零售。

entries.definition: Built on the same French verb for cutting off a share, here a small part described closely.
entries.definitionCN: 同样源自表切割的法语动词，指细述的小部分。

entries.definition: The stick with notches that lies behind the legal image.
entries.definitionCN: 背后刻缺口的木条，正是法律意象的来源。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for including as part; entail stresses necessity more.
entries.definitionCN: 表包含的日常动词，entail 更强调必然性。

entries.definition: To need by rule or nature, without the image of attached consequences.
entries.definitionCN: 按规则或本性需要，不含附带后果的意象。

entries.definition: To make necessary, a formal rival used in reports.
entries.definitionCN: 使成为必需，是报告语体中的正式竞争词。

entries.definition: To take something as a condition before it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物事先当作条件。

normalIntro.en: Entail can be read as en plus tail: a duty follows at the tail of every action.
normalIntro.cn: entail 可读作 en 加 tail：每项行动的尾巴上都跟着义务。

normal.en: Subject is a task or situation; object is the attached cost or labour.
normal.cn: 主语多为任务或情境，宾语为附带的代价或劳动。

normal.en: Entail takes a noun or an -ing form, never an infinitive.
normal.cn: entail 接名词或动名词，不接不定式。

normal.en: In law the noun entailment and the verb both keep the inheritance sense.
normal.cn: 法律上名词 entailment 与动词都保留继承义。

normal.en: Reports prefer entails to involves when the point is unavoidable cost.
normal.cn: 强调不可避免的代价时，报告体更用 entails。

normal.en: Remember the tail image: what hangs behind the action.
normal.cn: 记住尾巴意象：挂在行动之后的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a wagon hooked behind a horse that did not ask for it.
abstract.cn: 想象马身后被挂上一辆它并未要求的货车。

abstract.en: Imagine a tally stick whose notches bind the next heir.
abstract.cn: 想象刻着缺口、束缚下一位继承人的计数木条。

abstract.en: Think of a price tag sewn inside the collar of a new plan.
abstract.cn: 想想新方案领口内缝着的价签。

examples.en: The redesign entails rewriting every test.
examples.cn: 重新设计意味着重写所有测试。

examples.en: Such a merger would entail heavy legal costs.
examples.cn: 这样的合并将带来高昂的法律费用。

examples.en: Teaching young children entails patience above all.
examples.cn: 教幼儿最需要的品质是耐心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因台尔」——因为台上一句话，台下要跑腿，所以 entail 是牵涉、需要；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 高卢罗马语 *taxiare → 古法语 tailler（切）＋ en- → 盎格鲁-诺曼法语 entailler（为产业切定继承人）→ 中古英语 entaillen → 现代英语 entail，核心义「附带而不可分」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb grew out of a legal device for binding inheritance and now names anything that unavoidably comes attached.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词源于绑定继承的法律手段，如今指任何必然附随而来的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tail that cannot be cut off from the body of the plan.
core.cn: 核心意象：无法从计划主体上割下的尾巴。

branches.en: Any plan carries parts that cannot be avoided.
branches.cn: 任何计划都带有无法回避的部分。

branches.en: When the attached part is cost, the verb means demand.
branches.cn: 附随之物是代价时，动词转为要求。

branches.en: The legal sense binds heirs to an estate.
branches.cn: 法律义把继承人与产业绑定。

branches.en: Both describe a link that cannot be broken.
branches.cn: 两者都描述无法切断的关联。

branches.en: Obligation appears in budgets and in inheritance alike.
branches.cn: 义务既出现在预算中，也出现在继承中。

intro.en: A French prefix joins a French verb stem, and the family extends with English nominal endings.
intro.cn: 法语前缀接法语动词词干，词族由英语名词词尾延伸。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin taxare means to assess or arrange by notches, the learned ancestor of the French stem.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 taxare 指以刻痕估价或整理，是法语词干的书面前身。

items.exampleCN: en- 位于 entail 开头。

items.example: Taille names the mark cut in wood.
items.exampleCN: taille 指在木上刻出的记号。

items.example: The phrase records the original use.
items.exampleCN: 该短语记录了最初用法。

items.meaning: a binding condition or logical relation
items.example: Entailment is used in logic texts.

items.meaning: a small part cut off and described
items.exampleCN: detail 与 entail 共享法语词干。

definition_zh: n. 填字游戏
definition_en: a word puzzle played on a grid of squares
core_image: 黑白方格交错，词与词在格子里咬合
scene: 爷爷每天早上都做填字游戏。 Grandpa does the crossword every morning.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：crossword 指填字游戏；句意是爷爷每天早上都做填字游戏。

pos.zh: 填字游戏

senses.title: The puzzle
senses.definition: a puzzle in which words cross on a grid
senses.definitionCN: 词语在方格上交错的谜题
senses.example: She finished the crossword in ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 她十分钟就做完了填字游戏。
senses.why: Words locking into a grid.
senses.whyCN: 咬进方格的词。

senses.title: The grid
senses.definition: the pattern of white and black squares
senses.definitionCN: 黑白方格组成的版式
senses.example: The crossword had one black square.
senses.exampleCN: 这个填字游戏只有一个黑格。
senses.why: Black squares like gaps in a wall.
senses.whyCN: 像墙缝一样的黑格。

senses.title: A cryptic form
senses.definition: a harder version with tricky clues
senses.definitionCN: 提示曲折的难版

definition_zh: 倾向于……的；有某种爱好的；倾斜的；有坡度的
definition_en: likely or willing to do something, or resting at an angle rather than upright
core_image: 一块木板斜搭在石阶上，板面顺出一个缓坡；坡上站着的人没往下滑，反而很自然地想沿坡往上走
scene: 晚饭后客厅的话题转到搬家，母亲没有明确表态，只把杯子往儿子那边推了推，意思已经很清楚。 The committee was inclined to approve the plan after hearing the cost estimate.
sceneCN: 这里本词指倾向于做某事的（第 1 个义项：心里更可能选择某一边）；句意为听完成本估算后，委员会倾向于批准该方案。

senses.title: Ready to choose one course
senses.definition: likely or willing to do something rather than something else
senses.definitionCN: 更可能或更愿意做某事而非另一事
senses.example: The committee was inclined to approve the plan after hearing the cost estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 听完成本估算后，委员会倾向于批准该方案。
senses.why: The participle turns a leaning into a disposition: the mind has already bent toward one answer.
senses.whyCN: 分词把「倾斜」变成一种性情：心已经朝某一个答案弯过去了。

senses.title: Having a taste for something
senses.definition: naturally interested in a subject or activity and often good at it
senses.definitionCN: 对某学科或活动天性感兴趣，且往往擅长
senses.example: She is musically inclined and plays three instruments.
senses.exampleCN: 她有音乐方面的爱好，会演奏三种乐器。
senses.why: A taste is a mind leaning without pressure, so the same participle covers liking as well as choice.
senses.whyCN: 爱好是不受压力的心思偏向，因此同一分词既能指选择，也能指喜爱。

senses.title: Resting at an angle
senses.definition: positioned at an angle between the horizontal and the vertical
senses.definitionCN: 处在水平与竖直之间的角度上
senses.example: The lamp stood inclined against the wall, throwing light upward.
senses.exampleCN: 台灯斜靠在墙上，把光往上打。
senses.why: This is the literal old sense: a body that has bent away from straight up.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的古老义：物体已经从竖直方向弯开。

senses.title: Built as a slope
senses.definition: having a surface that rises or falls at a steady angle
senses.definitionCN: 表面以稳定角度上升或下降的
senses.example: Goods travelled down an inclined chute to the lower floor.
senses.exampleCN: 货物沿一条斜槽滑到下层。
senses.why: A slope put to work becomes an inclined plane, one of the simple machines.
senses.whyCN: 把斜坡派上用场就成了斜面，即简单机械之一。

senses.title: Leaning one way politically
senses.definition: favouring one party, camp or policy over the others
senses.definitionCN: 在党派、阵营或政策上更偏向某一边
senses.example: The paper is widely thought to be inclined toward the ruling party.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报纸被普遍认为偏向执政党。
senses.why: A mind that leans needs no push, so political sympathy is described with the same participle.
senses.whyCN: 心会自己倾过去，无需推力，因此政治上的同情也用同一分词描述。

senses.title: Likely to suffer from something
senses.definition: more likely than others to develop a particular illness or condition
senses.definitionCN: 比他人更容易出现某种疾病或状况
senses.example: People with that gene are inclined to early hearing loss.
senses.exampleCN: 携带该基因的人易出现早发性听力下降。
senses.why: A body leaning toward a weakness is treated as a statistical tilt, and the participle carries over.
senses.whyCN: 身体朝某种弱点倾去，被当作统计意义上的倾斜，分词就沿用过来。

senses.title: Showing a natural bent for something
senses.definition: showing a natural ability or disposition in a particular direction
senses.definitionCN: 在某一方向上显出天生的能力或倾向
senses.example: He is inclined toward mathematics rather than languages.
senses.exampleCN: 他天生更倾向数学而非语言。
senses.why: The leaning is inborn here, so the participle points to a bent rather than a decision.
senses.whyCN: 这里的倾向是天生带来的，分词指的是天资的偏斜而非决定。

senses.title: Holding a certain opinion
senses.definition: having a view that leans toward one conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 持有的看法更靠近某一结论
senses.example: Most economists are inclined to see the slowdown as temporary.
senses.exampleCN: 多数经济学家倾向于认为这次放缓是暂时的。
senses.why: An opinion is a mind at rest at an angle, and the participle describes where it rests.
senses.whyCN: 看法是心停在某个角度上，分词描述的正是它停在哪里。

intro.en: Inclined is the past participle of incline, from Latin inclinare 'to bend towards', itself in- plus clinare 'to bend'.
intro.cn: 本词是同族动词的过去分词，该动词来自拉丁语 inclinare「朝某方向弯」，由表方向的前缀加 clinare「弯」构成。

items.en: Clinare meant 'to bend, to cause to lean', used of bodies rather than of opinions.
items.cn: clinare 意为「弯、使倾」，用于物体，不用于意见。

items.en: Latin in- gave the verb a direction, so inclinare meant 'to bend towards something'.
items.cn: 拉丁语表方向的前缀为动词指明方向，故意为「朝某物弯过去」。

items.en: English took the verb through French, first for physical leaning and then for leaning of the will.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入该动词，先用于物理倾斜，再用于意志的偏向。

items.en: The participle became an adjective, so a person can be described as bent toward a choice, a taste or an opinion.
items.cn: 分词转为形容词，于是一个人便可被说成朝某个选择、某种爱好或某个看法弯过去。

items.en: Law, medicine and politics use the adjective for likelihood, risk and sympathy, each preserving the image of a tilt.
items.cn: 法律、医学与政治用该形容词表示可能性、风险与同情，各自保留倾斜的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the English verb is recorded from the fourteenth century, while the older base behind clinare is generally considered a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：英语动词的书记始于十四世纪，而 clinare 背后的更早词基一般认为是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms that look close and are often mistaken for the participle; group two holds adjectives of willingness and slope.
note.cn: 第一组是与本分词形近、常被误用的形式；第二组是表示意愿与坡度的形容词。

entries.definition: The base verb meaning to lean or to make someone willing; the past participle adds the settled result.
entries.definitionCN: 基干动词，意为倾斜或使某人愿意；过去分词则加出「已定」的结果。

entries.definition: The noun naming the leaning or the tendency; the adjective describes a person or thing that leans.
entries.definitionCN: 命名倾斜或倾向的名词；本词描述会倾的人或物。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone who can be talked round, built with a suffix of possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 以表可能性的后缀构成，指可以被说动的人。

entries.definition: The present participle describing a leaning under way; the past participle describes a settled angle.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，描述正在发生的倾斜；过去分词描述的则是已定的角度。

entries.definition: Often followed by a verb, it marks a usual direction of behaviour rather than a single willingness.
entries.definitionCN: 常接动词，标出行为的通常走向，而非某一次的意愿。

entries.definition: Stressing consent without resistance; inclined may be only a likelihood, not a promise.
entries.definitionCN: 强调同意而不抗拒；本词可能只是可能性，并非承诺。

entries.definition: Describing a surface that falls away; it says nothing about what anyone wants.
entries.definitionCN: 描述向下倾斜的表面；不涉及任何人的意愿。

entries.definition: Having a weight thrown to one side, usually with disapproval; inclined is milder.
entries.definitionCN: 重量被压向一边，通常带贬义；本词语气较轻。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The participle form of a real family: incline, inclined, inclination, inclinable.
normal.cn: 一个真实词族的分词形式：使倾斜、倾向于、倾向、易被说动的。

normal.en: Fixed patterns: be inclined to do, be inclined toward, an inclined plane.
normal.cn: 固定结构：倾向于做、偏向……、斜面。

normal.en: Both a mind and a board can be described by it, which is why the word feels physical and mental at once.
normal.cn: 心和木板都能用它形容，所以这个词同时带着物理与心理两种质地。

normal.en: Everyday phrases such as artistically inclined or mathematically inclined name a taste, not a decision.
normal.cn: 如「有艺术爱好」「有数学天分」这类日常说法命名的是爱好，不是决定。

normal.en: The verb takes a to-infinitive for a choice and a preposition for a taste or an opinion.
normal.cn: 接不定式指选择，接介词指爱好或看法。

abstract.en: Picture a plank laid on stone steps so that a slow slope is made on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木板搭在石阶上，有意搭出一道缓坡。

abstract.en: Picture a whole room leaning toward one answer before anyone speaks it aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象满屋子人都朝同一个答案偏着，还没人把它说出声。

abstract.en: Picture a cup pushed a few centimetres across a table as the only reply.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子在桌面上被推出几厘米，就算唯一的回答。

examples.en: I am inclined to think the delay was unavoidable.
examples.cn: 我倾向于认为这次延误无可避免。

examples.en: The road is inclined steeply for the last kilometre.
examples.cn: 最后一段路坡度很陡。

examples.en: She is inclined toward the arts rather than the sciences.
examples.cn: 她更偏向艺术而非科学。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one participle: a mind bent toward a choice, a taste, a body at an angle, a built slope, a political lean, a bodily risk, an inborn bent and a held opinion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个分词展开：心朝选择弯、朝爱好弯、身体成角、筑成斜坡、政治偏向、身体风险、天生偏向和持有的看法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plank laid across stone steps, making a slope that invites walking up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块木板搭在石阶上，形成一道引人往上走的坡。

branches.en: THE LEANING MIND: willingness and a settled opinion are the same tilt before and after a decision.
branches.cn: 倾的心：意愿与定见，是决定前后同一种倾斜。

branches.en: TASTE AND GIFT: a liking and an inborn bent both arrive without being chosen.
branches.cn: 爱好与天资：喜爱与天生偏向都不由选择而来。

branches.en: BODY AND GROUND: a thing resting at an angle and a slope built to be used.
branches.cn: 物与地：以角度停着的物体，与被人造出来使用的斜坡。

branches.en: THE POLITICAL LEAN: sympathy for one camp is a leaning the word can name.
branches.cn: 政治的偏：对某一阵营的同情，正是这个词能命名的倾斜。

branches.en: THE BODY'S RISK: a tendency to illness is a statistical tilt of the flesh.
branches.cn: 身体的风险：易患某病是肉体在统计意义上的倾斜。

intro.en: Inclined is a past participle used as an adjective; its base verb is built from a prefix and a bending verb, and those parts recur in the whole family.
intro.cn: 本词是作形容词用的过去分词；其动词由表方向的前缀与表「弯」的动词构成，这些部分贯穿整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- supplies direction, clinare supplies the bend, and the participle ending marks a completed state; English adds nothing further.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表方向的前缀提供方向，表「弯」的动词提供弯曲义，分词词尾标示已完成的状态；英语不再另加成分。

items.exampleCN: 该动词曾用于桅杆与身体。

items.example: The prefixed verb gave the bend a direction.
items.exampleCN: 加前缀后，弯曲有了方向。

items.example: The board is inclined at twelve degrees.
The path inclines toward the mill.

items.exampleCN: 他似乎对这提议有点动心。
